sessions.goal: Do 30 push-ups in a row within 8 weeks. I can do about 8 rig

protocol.goal_statement: Go from ~8 clean push-ups to 30 unbroken in 8 weeks, training 4 mornings a week at home.
protocol.short_title: 30 push-ups in a row in 8 weeks

phases.title: Build the base
phases.focus: Four short morning sessions a week, sets that stop well short of failure, a written record of every set, and enough protein and sleep to actually build the reps.

steps.title: Morning push-up session
steps.details: Four mornings a week, first thing before the day starts. Do 5 sets of 4 reps, resting 60-90 seconds between sets. Stop each set while you still have 3 good reps left in you — none of these sets should be a fight. Two or three easy warm-up sets of 5 before the working sets. If a set starts to look ugly, end it there.

how_to.gist: 5 sets of 4 reps, 60-90 seconds rest, stopping 3 reps short of failure.
how_to.why: You can do 8 in a row now, so 4 at a time feels almost silly — that's the point. This is how you pile up reps without wrecking yourself for the next morning.

sections.heading: The session
items: Stop each set with 3 good reps still in the tank

sections.heading: Where
sections.body: On the floor at home, in the morning before anything else gets a claim on your day. Same spot every time so there's nothing to decide.

sections.heading: The rule
sections.body: None of these sets should be a fight. If rep 4 of a set is a grind, you went too hard — cut the set short and keep the rest of the session as planned.

how_to.counts_as_done: All 5 sets of 4 done, any time that morning.

steps.week_progression: Week 1: 5x4. Week 2: 5x5.

steps.title: Write down every set
steps.details: Right after each session, jot the reps of every set in your phone notes — '5,5,4,4,4' is enough. Next session, aim to beat one set by a single rep. This is the whole engine of the plan: reps only climb if you know what you did last time.

how_to.gist: Log the reps of each set right after the session, then beat one set next time.
how_to.why: Push-up progress is not magic — it's doing slightly more than last time. Without the numbers in front of you, every session becomes a guess and the curve flattens.

sections.heading: What to write
items: The reps of each set, in order
Anything that felt off — a sore wrist, a sloppy last rep

sections.heading: How to use it
sections.body: Before you start, glance at last session's numbers. Your only job today is to beat one of those sets by one rep. Not all of them — one.

sections.heading: Where
sections.body: Phone notes, a notebook by the mat, whatever is already open in the morning. Ten seconds of writing, not a spreadsheet.

how_to.counts_as_done: Today's set reps are written down.

steps.week_progression: Same habit all eight weeks — the numbers in it are what change.

steps.title: Hit ~150 g protein
steps.details: Aim for about 150 g of protein a day — roughly a palm-sized portion at every meal plus a shake. That's the amount that keeps the muscle you're building instead of letting the extra training eat into it. If you weigh noticeably more or less than 170 lb, adjust up or down by about 10 g per 20 lb.

how_to.gist: About 150 g of protein a day — a palm at every meal plus a shake.
how_to.why: Push-ups are a strength exercise, and strength gains need building blocks. Protein is the one food number that actually changes how fast the reps climb.

sections.heading: The target
sections.body: ~150 g a day. This is scaled to a bodyweight of about 170 lb — if that's off, correct it in the app and the number moves with you.

sections.heading: How to hit it
items: Palm-sized protein portion at breakfast, lunch and dinner
One shake or a tub of Greek yogurt as the top-up
Eggs, chicken, fish, beans, tofu — whatever you actually eat

sections.heading: Don't overthink it
sections.body: You don't need to weigh food. Three solid protein portions plus one shake lands most people in the right range.

how_to.counts_as_done: Three protein portions plus a shake, or the equivalent, eaten today.

steps.week_progression: Same target all eight weeks.

steps.title: One full rest day between sessions
steps.details: Wednesday, Saturday and Sunday are push-up-free. No 'just a quick set' on those days — the reps you're chasing are built while you're not training. Walk, stretch, do whatever else you like; just don't add push-ups.

how_to.gist: No push-ups on Wednesday, Saturday or Sunday. Not even one set.
how_to.why: Four mornings a week is the right dose. Adding reps on rest days is the single most common way this plan stalls — you feel fine for a week, then everything gets heavy at once.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.body: Muscle gets stronger between sessions, not during them. Wednesday sits right in the middle of your training week for exactly that reason.

sections.heading: If you're itching to move
sections.body: Walk, stretch, do something else entirely. Just keep the push-ups off the calendar on these three days.

how_to.counts_as_done: No push-up sets done on the rest day.

steps.week_progression: Unchanged across all eight weeks.

steps.title: In bed by 11pm on training nights
steps.details: Lights out by 11pm the night before each morning session, aiming for 7-8 hours. Set an alarm for the wind-down, not just the wake-up. If you're training at 6am, that means screens off and phone charging in another room by 10:30.

how_to.gist: Lights out by 11pm the night before every morning session.
how_to.why: Four mornings a week only works if the mornings aren't a fight. Sleep is where the reps you did actually turn into strength — and it's the first thing to go when a plan gets busy.

sections.heading: The target
sections.body: 7-8 hours. If your session is at 6am, that's lights out at 10:30-11pm, not 11:30.

sections.heading: The wind-down
items: 10:00pm — alarm goes off to start winding down
10:30pm — phone on the charger, in another room

sections.heading: If you miss it
sections.body: Do the session anyway, just at a slightly easier level — drop one set. One short night is noise; three in a row is what flattens the week.

how_to.counts_as_done: Lights out by 11pm the night before a training morning.

steps.week_progression: Same target all eight weeks.

phases.title: Add volume
phases.focus: More reps per set and a first real measurement at the end of week 4 — still never training to failure.

steps.title: Morning push-up session
steps.details: Same four mornings, more work. Do 5 sets of 7 reps with 75-90 seconds rest, still stopping 2-3 reps short of failure. Warm up with 2-3 easy sets of 5 first. If the last set drops below 6 clean reps, cut the session there and note it.

how_to.gist: 5 sets of 7 reps, 75-90 seconds rest, still 2-3 reps in reserve.
how_to.why: Your total weekly reps roughly double in these two weeks. That's the jump that makes 20 in a row feel ordinary by week 5.

sections.heading: The rule
sections.body: If your last set falls below 6 clean reps, end the session there. That's information, not failure — write it down and repeat the same numbers next time.

sections.heading: If it feels easy
sections.body: Good. Add one rep to one set next session. Never add reps to all five sets at once.

how_to.counts_as_done: All 5 sets done, any time that morning.

steps.week_progression: Week 3: 5x6. Week 4: 5x7, then retest.

steps.title: Write down every set
steps.details: Same habit as before, and it matters more now — the sets are close enough to your limit that guessing won't work. Note the reps of each set and beat one set by a rep next session.

how_to.gist: Log every set's reps, then beat one set by a rep next time.
how_to.why: At 7 reps a set you're close enough to your edge that 'I think I did about the same' stops being good enough. The numbers are how you know.

sections.heading: What to write
items: Reps of each set, in order

sections.heading: How to use it
sections.body: One rep better on one set. That's the whole target for the next session.

how_to.counts_as_done: Today's set reps are written down.

steps.week_progression: Same habit; the numbers climb.

steps.title: Finish each session with 2 easy sets
steps.details: Same 2 sets of 5, but now with hands on a low step or the edge of a sofa instead of a chair — a bit lower, a bit harder. Easy reps only; if 5 feels hard, go back up a height.

how_to.gist: 2 sets of 5 with hands on a low step or sofa edge.
how_to.why: Lower hands mean more of your bodyweight on the arms — the same easy volume, now doing more work. This is how the support muscles keep pace with the pushing ones.

sections.heading: Setup
sections.body: Hands on a low step, a sofa edge, or a sturdy box. Lower than the chair you used in weeks 1-2.

sections.heading: If it hurts
sections.body: Sharp pain — stop, go back to the higher surface for the rest of the week.

how_to.counts_as_done: Both easy sets done after the working sets.

steps.week_progression: Lower the surface again in phase 3 if 5 reps still feels easy.

steps.title: Week 4: test your max once
steps.details: On the Friday of week 4, after a proper warm-up, do one set of push-ups to your honest limit and write the number down. This is the only max attempt in the first six weeks — everything else stays comfortably short of failure. Rest 3 minutes after your warm-up before you start.

how_to.gist: One all-out set on the Friday of week 4. Write the number down.
how_to.why: You need one real measurement to know whether the volume is working. Doing this weekly would wreck the plan; doing it once at the halfway point tells you whether to push harder or adjust.

sections.heading: How to do it
items: Warm up with 2 easy sets of 5
One set, as many clean reps as you can
Stop the moment your form breaks — that's the number

sections.heading: What counts
sections.body: Clean reps only. Chest to within a fist of the floor, body straight, no bouncing. A sloppy rep doesn't count and never has.

sections.heading: What it means
sections.body: Somewhere in the mid-to-high teens is on track. If you're still at 10-12, keep going — the last stretch of this plan is where the biggest jumps happen.

how_to.counts_as_done: One max set done and the number written down.

steps.week_progression: Week 4 only. Next test is week 8.

steps.title: In bed by 11pm on training nights
steps.details: Same rule as before, and it's carrying more weight now — the sessions are harder and recovery is what turns them into strength. Lights out by 11pm, 7-8 hours, phone charging in another room.

how_to.gist: Lights out by 11pm the night before every morning session.
how_to.why: The sessions get harder in these two weeks. Sleep is the difference between adapting to them and just accumulating fatigue.

sections.heading: The target
sections.body: 7-8 hours, lights out by 11pm.

sections.heading: If you miss it
sections.body: Train anyway, one set lighter. Two short nights in a row is the point where you drop a session rather than grind through it.

how_to.counts_as_done: Lights out by 11pm the night before a training morning.

steps.week_progression: Same target.

phases.title: Push the ceiling
phases.focus: Longer sets, fewer of them, and the first time you string together reps that start to look like the real thing.

steps.title: Morning push-up session
steps.details: Four mornings, now built around longer sets. Do 4 sets of 10 reps with 2 minutes rest, stopping 2 reps short of failure. Warm up with 2 easy sets of 5. If a set drops below 8 clean reps, stop the session and repeat the same numbers next time.

how_to.gist: 4 sets of 10 reps, 2 minutes rest, 2 reps in reserve.
how_to.why: Ten in a row is more than you could do when you started. Sets this long are what teach your body to keep going past the point where it used to quit.

sections.heading: The rule
sections.body: Below 8 clean reps in a set means the session is over. Write it down and repeat the same numbers next time rather than pushing through.

sections.heading: Pace
sections.body: Steady, not fast. Rushing the reps is what makes the last ones sloppy.

how_to.counts_as_done: All 4 sets done, any time that morning.

steps.week_progression: Week 5: 4x9. Week 6: 4x10.

steps.title: Write down every set
steps.details: Same habit. With sets of 9-10 reps, one rep added to one set is a real gain — chase that, not a whole new session.

how_to.gist: Log every set's reps, then beat one set by a rep next time.
how_to.why: At this stage a single rep is a real improvement. The log is what turns 'that felt hard' into a decision about what to do next session.

sections.heading: What to write
items: Reps of each set, in order

sections.heading: How to use it
sections.body: One rep better on one set next time. If two sessions in a row you can't beat anything, drop back to the previous week's numbers for a week.

how_to.counts_as_done: Today's set reps are written down.

steps.week_progression: Same habit.

steps.title: Finish each session with 2 easy sets
steps.details: 2 sets of 8 now, hands on the floor if you can manage them cleanly, otherwise on a low step. These are the last reps of the session and they should feel light — if they don't, put your hands back up a level.

how_to.gist: 2 sets of 8 easy reps, hands on the floor if they stay clean.
how_to.why: Extra easy reps at the end add volume without adding strain. By now your shoulders can usually handle the full position for short sets like these.

sections.heading: The sets
items: Hands on the floor, or a low step if the floor version gets ugly

sections.heading: The rule
sections.body: These must feel easy. The moment they don't, raise your hands back up — the point is extra reps, not extra fatigue.

how_to.counts_as_done: Both easy sets done after the working sets.

steps.week_progression: Weeks 5-6: 2x8. Phase 4 keeps them but shorter.

steps.title: One full rest day between sessions
steps.details: Wednesday, Saturday, Sunday — no push-ups. This matters more now than it did in week 1: the sets are long enough that your shoulders and triceps need the gap to come back.

how_to.gist: No push-ups on Wednesday, Saturday or Sunday.
how_to.why: Longer sets mean more recovery needed, not less. The rest days are doing as much for your max as the training days are.

sections.heading: If you're itching to move
sections.body: Walk, stretch, do something else. Just no push-up sets.

how_to.counts_as_done: No push-up sets done on the rest day.

steps.week_progression: Unchanged.

steps.title: In bed by 11pm on training nights
steps.details: Same rule. Sets of 10 take more out of you than sets of 4 did — the sleep is what makes the next morning's session possible rather than miserable.

how_to.gist: Lights out by 11pm the night before every morning session.
how_to.why: This is the phase where the sessions get genuinely hard. Short sleep now shows up as sets that collapse two reps early.

sections.heading: The target
sections.body: 7-8 hours, lights out by 11pm.

how_to.counts_as_done: Lights out by 11pm the night before a training morning.

steps.week_progression: Same target.

phases.title: Go for 30
phases.focus: Shorter, sharper sessions that protect your freshness, then one honest attempt at 30 in the final week.

steps.title: Morning push-up session
steps.details: Four mornings, but shorter and sharper so you arrive at the final test fresh. Do 3 sets of 12 reps with 2-3 minutes rest, stopping 2 reps short of failure. Warm up with 2 easy sets of 5. Week 8: cut to 3 sets of 8 from Wednesday onward so your arms are fresh for the test.

how_to.gist: 3 sets of 12, 2-3 minutes rest — then taper down in the last few days.
how_to.why: You don't get stronger in the final week, you get fresher. The work is already banked; these sessions just keep the pattern sharp without draining you.

sections.heading: The rule
sections.body: Nothing in this phase should leave you sore the next day. If it does, cut a set.

how_to.counts_as_done: The session done as written for that week.

steps.week_progression: Week 7: 3x12. Week 8: taper to 3x8 then 2x8.

steps.title: Write down every set
steps.details: Keep logging, including the taper week — knowing exactly how fresh you are going into the test is worth more than any extra set.

how_to.gist: Keep logging every set, including the easy taper week.
how_to.why: The log tells you whether you're arriving at the test fresh or tired. That's the difference between a good attempt and a wasted one.

sections.heading: What to write
items: How easy it felt, in one word

sections.heading: How to use it
sections.body: If the taper week still feels heavy, take an extra rest day before the test. Fresh beats prepared.

how_to.counts_as_done: Today's set reps are written down.

steps.week_progression: Same habit.

steps.title: One full rest day between sessions
steps.details: Wednesday, Saturday, Sunday off, no exceptions — and in week 8, take Saturday and Sunday completely off before the final attempt.

how_to.gist: No push-ups Wednesday, Saturday or Sunday.
how_to.why: Rest days are what make the final attempt possible. Two full days off before the test is not laziness, it's the plan.

sections.heading: Before the test
sections.body: Take the two days before your attempt completely off from push-ups. Walk if you want. Nothing else.

how_to.counts_as_done: No push-up sets done on the rest day.

steps.week_progression: Unchanged.

steps.title: Week 8: go for 30
steps.details: On the Friday of week 8, after two easy days off and a proper warm-up, do one set of push-ups and don't stop until you hit 30 or your form breaks. Warm up with 2 easy sets of 5, rest 3 minutes, then go. Steady rhythm, no rushing — the people who fail at 26 are the ones who sprinted the first 10.

how_to.gist: One all-out set on the Friday of week 8. Target: 30 clean reps.
how_to.why: This is the whole point of the eight weeks. Everything before it was building the capacity for this one set.

sections.heading: Before you start
items: Water, and a clear count in your head

sections.heading: The set
sections.body: Steady rhythm from rep one. If you can talk yourself into a fast start, don't — the first 10 should feel almost boring. Break it into chunks of 5 in your head if that helps.

sections.heading: If you fall short
sections.body: Write the number down. Anything in the high 20s after starting at 8 is a real result, and a second attempt three days later often beats the first — most people's best set comes on the second try.

how_to.counts_as_done: One max set done and the number written down.

steps.week_progression: Week 8 only.

steps.title: In bed by 11pm on training nights
steps.details: Same rule, and it's the cheapest thing you can do for the final attempt. Two good nights' sleep before Friday is worth more than any extra set you could squeeze in.

how_to.gist: Lights out by 11pm the night before every morning session.
how_to.why: The final attempt is a single set. Sleep is the one thing that reliably adds reps to a single set.

sections.heading: The target
sections.body: 7-8 hours, lights out by 11pm — and especially the two nights before the test.

how_to.counts_as_done: Lights out by 11pm the night before a training morning.

steps.week_progression: Same target.

milestones.title: Two weeks, eight sessions, zero missed
milestones.criteria: You've done all four morning sessions in both weeks 1 and 2, and every set is written down. Sets of 5 that felt like a warm-up at the start now feel routine.

milestones.title: First real measurement
milestones.criteria: Week 4's max test is done and written down. Whatever the number is, it's higher than 8 — and you now know exactly what the volume is buying you.

milestones.title: Ten in a row is a normal set
milestones.criteria: You're doing 4 sets of 10 in a single morning, stopping short of failure. A set of 10 no longer feels like a max — it feels like Tuesday.

milestones.title: 30 unbroken
milestones.criteria: One set, 30 clean push-ups, chest to the floor, body straight. Written down and done.

protocol.coach_notes: The first 15 reps of this will come faster than you expect and the last 5 will feel like they're nailed to the floor — that's normal, and it's why the plan never asks you to test your max until week 4. Four mornings a week is the whole engine here; miss one and nothing happens, miss two in a row and the curve flattens for a fortnight. So the rule is simple: never miss twice. The rep after a miss is the one that decides whether this works.

sessions.goal: Read a lot more this year — I keep buying books and not read

protocol.goal_statement: Read 10 pages in bed at 10:30 on weeknights, phone charging in the kitchen overnight, plus one audiobook chapter on the Saturday walk
protocol.short_title: Read 10 pages a night for 12 weeks

phases.title: Ten pages, phone in the kitchen
phases.focus: Get the book open at 10:30 on weeknights and the phone out of the bedroom — nothing else changes yet.

steps.title: Read 10 pages in bed
steps.details: In bed, lights on, book open. Ten pages is about fifteen minutes. The count restarts each night — you don't carry pages over from a night you missed.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 1-2: ten pages, no more expected. Weeks 3-4: still ten pages — the win is that it stops feeling like a decision.

how_to.gist: In bed with the book open, read ten pages before you turn the light off.
how_to.why: This is the whole plan. Ten pages a night is roughly fifteen minutes, and fifteen minutes a night is a book every three or four weeks — which is the difference between buying books and reading them.

sections.heading: The setup
sections.body: Book on the pillow before dinner, not on the shelf. Phone already in the kitchen. You get into bed, you pick up the book — there's no decision to make at 10:30, because the decision was made at seven.

sections.heading: The count
sections.body: Ten pages, counted from wherever you open to. If you're mid-chapter and want to keep going, keep going — the ten is a floor, not a ceiling. If you're at page four and your eyes are closing, that's four pages and it still counts as a night in bed with the book.

sections.heading: If it's late
sections.body: Home at 11, exhausted, ten pages feels like a wall? Read two pages. Two pages keeps the night alive and keeps the chain going. The only thing that breaks this is not opening the book at all.

how_to.counts_as_done: Ten pages read in bed, or any honest attempt at the book after 10:30 — the app shows the night checked.

steps.title: Phone charging in the kitchen overnight
steps.details: Phone goes on the kitchen charger when you go up to bed and stays there until morning. That means an actual charger in the kitchen — not a cable you have to go find.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 1-2: every night, including weekends. Weeks 3-4: same, and it should now take no thought at all.

how_to.gist: Phone on the kitchen charger when you head up to bed — every night.
how_to.why: The phone within arm's reach at 10:30 is what's been beating you. You can't read a book and scroll at the same time, so the simplest fix is to make the scroll impossible rather than resist it.

sections.heading: Set it up once
items: A charger plugged in and living on the kitchen counter — not borrowed from the bedroom
A cheap alarm clock in the bedroom so the phone isn't your alarm
Your watch or the clock is what wakes you now

sections.heading: The routine
sections.body: When you stand up to go to bed, the phone goes on the kitchen charger on the way past. It's the same motion as turning off the kitchen light. It stays there until morning — no 'just checking one thing' trips back down.

sections.heading: The hard part
sections.body: The first three or four nights you'll feel the missing phone like a missing limb. That's the point, and it fades. If you genuinely need it for something at night, get it, do the thing, and put it straight back — don't bring it upstairs.

how_to.counts_as_done: Phone spent the night on the kitchen charger and you woke up without it beside the bed.

steps.title: In bed with the book by 10:30
steps.details: 10:30 is lights-on-with-a-book, not lights-out. Getting into bed at 10:30 with the book already there is the whole move — the reading follows from it.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 1-2: aim for 10:30, land anywhere before 11 and call it a win. Weeks 3-4: 10:30 becomes the actual time you're in bed with the book.

how_to.gist: In bed, book in hand, by 10:30 on weeknights.
how_to.why: A fixed time beats a daily intention every week. 'I'll read tonight' has no edge to it; 10:30 does — and it's early enough that ten pages doesn't eat your sleep.

sections.heading: Work backwards
items: 10:15 — upstairs, teeth brushed, phone on the kitchen charger

sections.heading: The rule
sections.body: 10:30 means in bed with the book, not lights out. If you're in bed at 10:30 and read until 10:50, you've done it perfectly. If you get in at 10:55, you've still done it — just note that the late nights are the ones that turn into no nights.

sections.heading: Weekends
sections.body: Weeknights only. Friday night counts as a weeknight here if that's how your week runs — pick your five and keep them the same five.

how_to.counts_as_done: You were in bed with the book by 10:30 (or close enough that you read that night).

steps.title: One audiobook chapter on the Saturday walk
steps.details: Headphones in, audiobook on, one chapter on your Saturday walk. This is the easy on-ramp — no bed, no clock, no willpower, just a walk you were taking anyway.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 1-4: one chapter. If the walk is longer than the chapter, keep listening — it's free pages.

how_to.gist: One audiobook chapter on your Saturday walk.
how_to.why: A second, easier way into the week. When weeknights go sideways — and some will — the Saturday chapter keeps the week from being a zero, and it keeps the whole thing feeling alive.

sections.heading: Before you leave
sections.body: Audiobook downloaded and queued the night before, headphones by the door with your shoes. Don't leave the house and then start browsing for something to listen to — that's how the walk ends in silence and a podcast.

sections.heading: The chapter
sections.body: One chapter, start to finish. If the walk is longer, keep going. If the chapter is long, listen to as much as the walk covers and pick it up next Saturday — audiobooks don't need to be finished in one go.

sections.heading: Same book or different
sections.body: Your call. Some people run one book in print and one in audio so the two never compete. Whatever keeps both going.

how_to.counts_as_done: One chapter listened on the Saturday walk.

steps.title: Three nights is a bad week, not a zero
steps.details: The floor for a week that work eats: three nights in bed with the book, and the Saturday chapter still counts as one of them. Last year's attempt died in week two because a busy week had no script — this is the script. Three nights keeps the habit alive without pretending a brutal week is a normal one.
steps.week_progression: Every week of the plan. On a normal week you'll clear five without thinking; this only matters on the weeks you don't.

how_to.gist: On a wrecked week, get to three nights — Saturday's chapter counts as one.
how_to.why: Your last attempt died in week two when work got busy, and nothing in the plan said what to do about it. A missed Tuesday isn't a verdict. Three nights is the minimum that keeps this alive, and naming it in advance is what stops a bad week from becoming the end of the plan.

sections.heading: The floor
sections.body: Three nights in bed with the book, any three, plus the Saturday chapter if you can get it. That's the bad-week minimum. Below that and the week has genuinely slipped.

sections.heading: How to use it
sections.body: You don't decide in advance that this is a bad week — you notice on Thursday that you've only read once, and you read Thursday and Friday. Two nights back to back is enough to keep the chain from snapping.

sections.heading: After a bad week
sections.body: Straight back to five the next week. No catching up on missed pages, no penance reading. The pages you didn't read are gone; the habit isn't.

how_to.counts_as_done: Three nights with the book in a week, or five — either way the week counts.

phases.title: Ten pages becomes fifteen
phases.focus: The habit has grip — now the reading gets a little longer and the book gets chosen on purpose.

steps.title: Read 15 pages in bed
steps.details: Same 10:30, same bed, same book — fifteen pages instead of ten. About twenty minutes. If a night runs long and fifteen is too much, ten still counts.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 5-6: fifteen pages. Weeks 7-8: fifteen pages, and if a book is gripping you, let it run past the count.

how_to.gist: Fifteen pages in bed at 10:30 on weeknights.
how_to.why: Ten pages got the habit installed. Fifteen is where reading starts to actually move through books — you'll finish something every two to three weeks instead of every month.

sections.heading: The bump
sections.body: Five more pages, about five more minutes. That's the whole change. Don't jump further than this — the point is that it stays easy enough to do on a Tuesday when you're tired.

sections.heading: When it's late
sections.body: Late night, fifteen feels like a lot? Read ten. Ten is still a full night and the chain stays intact.

how_to.counts_as_done: Fifteen pages read in bed, or ten on a night that ran late.

steps.title: Phone charging in the kitchen overnight
steps.details: Unchanged, and it should now be automatic. If you've started drifting back to the phone in bed, this is the step to look at first — it's the one doing the heavy lifting.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 5-8: every night, no exceptions creeping in.

steps.title: In bed with the book by 10:30
steps.details: Same fixed time. By now it should feel less like a rule and more like what Tuesday is.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 5-8: 10:30 as the real time, not the aspirational one.

steps.title: One audiobook chapter on the Saturday walk
steps.details: Same Saturday walk, one chapter. If you've been enjoying it, this is a good week to start a second audiobook so there's always something queued.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 5-8: one chapter, and keep the next one downloaded so you never start a walk with nothing to play.

steps.title: Three nights is a bad week, not a zero
steps.details: The floor holds all the way through. Three nights in bed with the book, Saturday's chapter counting as one of them.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 5-8: unchanged. The floor doesn't move up as the pages do — it's there for the weeks that go wrong.

steps.title: Pick the next book before you finish this one
steps.details: A book you're excited about, chosen and waiting, before the current one ends. The gap between books is where reading habits quietly die — you finish on a Sunday and by Wednesday you've read nothing because there's nothing to read.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 5-8: one book lined up at all times. Weeks 9-12: two, so there's never a gap.

how_to.gist: Have the next book chosen and on the shelf before you finish the current one.
how_to.why: You said you keep buying books and not reading them — so the shelf is already full. The risk isn't running out of books, it's finishing one and drifting for a week with nothing pulling you to bed at 10:30.

sections.heading: The rule
sections.body: When you're about two chapters from the end of a book, pick the next one and put it on your pillow-side stack. No gap.

sections.heading: Choosing
sections.body: Pick something you actually want to read, not something you think you should. A page-turner at 10:30 beats a worthy book you avoid.

how_to.counts_as_done: The next book is chosen and waiting before the current one is finished.

phases.title: Twenty pages and a finished book
phases.focus: The reading is real now — longer nights, and the first books actually getting finished.

steps.title: Read 20 pages in bed
steps.details: Twenty pages, about half an hour. Same 10:30, same bed. On a night that runs late, fifteen or ten still counts — the count is a target, not a test.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 9-10: twenty pages. Weeks 11-12: twenty pages, and let a good book run past it when it wants to.

how_to.gist: Twenty pages in bed at 10:30 on weeknights.
how_to.why: Twenty pages a night is a book every two weeks or so. This is the pace that turns 'I buy books' into 'I read books' — and it's only possible because the first eight weeks built the habit at ten and fifteen.

sections.heading: The bump
sections.body: Half an hour of reading. If you're in bed at 10:30, that's lights out around 11 — still a full night's sleep. If 10:30 is already a stretch, keep the time and let the pages be fifteen.

sections.heading: When it's late
sections.body: Ten pages on a wrecked night is a full win. The floor is still three nights, and the floor is what matters.

how_to.counts_as_done: Twenty pages read in bed, or a shorter honest read on a night that ran late.

steps.title: Phone charging in the kitchen overnight
steps.details: Twelve weeks in and this is the habit underneath the habit. It stays.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 9-12: every night. If it's held this long, it's yours now.

steps.title: In bed with the book by 10:30
steps.details: The fixed time that started all of this. Still 10:30, still weeknights.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 9-12: 10:30, and it should now be the time you're in bed rather than the time you aim for.

steps.title: One audiobook chapter on the Saturday walk
steps.details: Same Saturday walk, one chapter — the easy win that's been keeping bad weeks from being zeros.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 9-12: one chapter, and if you want more, a second walk midweek with headphones is a fine addition.

steps.title: Three nights is a bad week, not a zero
steps.details: The floor holds to the end. Three nights in bed with the book, Saturday's chapter counting as one.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 9-12: unchanged. It's the rule that outlasts the plan.

steps.title: Finish a book and start the next one
steps.details: By now you should be closing books and opening new ones. When you finish one, the next is already chosen and waiting — no gap, no drift.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 9-12: keep the chain of books unbroken. Two or three finished across the phase is the sign this has become how you read.

how_to.gist: Finish a book, then start the next one that's already waiting.
how_to.why: Finishing books is the whole point of the goal — and the gap between books is where reading habits quietly die. Having the next one ready means there's never a night with nothing to pull you to bed at 10:30.

sections.heading: The handoff
sections.body: Last page of one book, first page of the next on the following night. Not a week later — the next night.

sections.heading: If a book stalls
sections.body: Some books just don't take. If you've been on the same one for three weeks and you're dreading 10:30, put it down and start something else. Finishing a book you hate isn't reading, it's homework.

how_to.counts_as_done: A book finished and the next one started the following night.

milestones.title: Four weeks in — the phone sleeps in the kitchen
milestones.criteria: You've read in bed on at least three nights every week for four weeks, and the phone has spent every night on the kitchen charger. The 10:30 bedtime is starting to feel like a normal evening rather than a plan.

milestones.title: Fifteen pages a night and a book finished
milestones.criteria: You've held fifteen pages a night for four weeks, finished at least one book, and had the next one chosen before the last one ended. You've also had a busy week and come out of it with three nights rather than zero.

milestones.title: Twelve weeks — reading is just what you do at 10:30
milestones.criteria: Twenty pages a night on weeknights, the phone in the kitchen every night, the Saturday chapter every week, and at least two or three books finished across the twelve weeks. You've read on more nights than you've missed, and a bad week no longer ends anything.

protocol.coach_notes: You built this plan yourself, and that matters — the phone on the kitchen charger was the right diagnosis, because the phone at 10:30 was the thing actually beating you. The only change we made is the floor: three nights is a bad week, not a zero. That's the rule that was missing last year when work got busy in week two. One missed night is noise. The night after a miss is the one that decides whether this is a habit or another attempt — so read the next night, even two pages, and let the streak do the rest.

sessions.goal: Lose 10 lbs

protocol.goal_statement: Lose 10 lbs (about 4.5 kg) with daily walks, two gym sessions a week, and a simple protein-and-portion rule at meals

phases.title: Start the walk and the two gym days
phases.focus: Get the daily walk and both gym sessions happening, put three simple rules on your meals, and get to bed at a set time. Week one should feel almost too easy.

steps.title: Walk 20 minutes
steps.details: A 20-minute walk every day, at a pace where you could still hold a conversation. Lunch break, after work, or split into two 10s — whatever actually happens. Rain plan: indoors, mall, or a longer route under cover.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 1-2: 20 minutes. Weeks 3-4: 30 minutes.

how_to.gist: 20 minutes of walking, every day, at a pace you could chat through.
how_to.why: This is the cheapest lever you own. It burns a little every day, it's the one thing that never depends on motivation, and it's already built around your desk job.

sections.heading: When
items: Lunch break — walk before you eat, so it can't get pushed
After work — straight out the door before you sit down
Split it: 10 minutes at lunch, 10 after dinner

sections.heading: The pace
sections.body: Brisk enough that you're breathing a bit harder than sitting, slow enough that you could hold a conversation. If you're gasping, ease off. If you're strolling, pick it up.

sections.heading: Rain plan
sections.body: Bad weather is not a rest day. Walk indoors — a mall, a big store, a corridor loop — or take an umbrella and go. The point is the 20 minutes, not the scenery.

sections.heading: If you miss
sections.body: One missed day is noise. Walk the next day. Two in a row is how the whole thing quietly dies.

how_to.counts_as_done: 20 minutes of walking done today, in one block or two.

steps.title: Gym session — full body
steps.details: Two full-body sessions a week, Tuesday and Saturday. Each one: a squat or leg press, a push (bench or overhead press), a pull (row or lat pulldown), and a hip hinge (deadlift or Romanian deadlift). 3 sets of 8-12 reps each, 2-3 light warm-up sets before your working sets. Rest 60-90 seconds between sets.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 1-2: 2 sets per exercise, learning the movements. Weeks 3-4: 3 sets per exercise.

how_to.gist: Two full-body sessions a week — squat, push, pull, hinge, 3 sets of 8-12.
how_to.why: Walking and eating less will move the scale, but without lifting you lose muscle along with the fat. Two sessions a week is enough to keep what you've got while the fat comes off.

sections.heading: The four moves
items: Push: bench press or overhead press

sections.heading: Sets and reps
sections.body: 3 sets of 8-12 reps on each. Pick a weight where the last two reps of the last set are genuinely hard but you're not grinding to failure. Rest 60-90 seconds between sets. Do 2-3 light warm-up sets on your first exercise before the working sets.

sections.heading: The week
items: Any order — just get both in

sections.heading: If you miss
sections.body: Miss Tuesday, do it Wednesday or Thursday. Miss both, pick up next week — don't try to cram three sessions into Sunday.

how_to.counts_as_done: Both sessions done this week, any days, any order.

steps.title: Write down every set and beat last time
steps.details: In your phone notes or a small notebook, write the exercise, the weight, and the reps for every working set. Before each session, look at last time's numbers and beat one of them — one more rep, or 2.5 kg / 5 lbs more on your main lift.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 1-2: just get the numbers written down. Weeks 3-4: beat one number every session.

how_to.gist: Log every set, then beat one number from last session.
how_to.why: Muscle has no reason to stick around unless it's being asked for a little more each time. This one habit is what separates two gym days that work from two gym days that are just exercise.

sections.heading: What to write
items: The reps you got on each set

sections.heading: Before you start
sections.body: Open last session's notes. Pick one number to beat today — one extra rep on your top set, or 2.5 kg / 5 lbs more on your main lift. Just one. The rest stays the same.

sections.heading: When it stops moving
sections.body: If you can't beat anything two sessions running, that's normal — hold the weight and add a rep instead. If it's still stuck after three, drop the weight 10% and build back up.

how_to.counts_as_done: This session's sets written down, and one number from last time beaten.

steps.title: Protein at every meal
steps.details: Aim for about 140 g of protein a day, spread across your meals — roughly a palm-sized portion at breakfast, lunch, and dinner. Eggs, Greek yogurt, chicken, fish, beef, beans, lentils, tofu. A shake counts if you need to close the gap.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 1-2: get a protein source into every meal, don't count. Weeks 3-4: start roughly tallying toward 140 g.

how_to.gist: About 140 g of protein a day — a palm-sized portion at each meal.
how_to.why: Protein is what keeps you full between meals and keeps your muscle while the fat comes off. It's the single food change that does the most work here.

sections.heading: The target
sections.body: Around 140 g a day, scaled to the bodyweight you gave me. You don't need to weigh anything — a palm-sized portion of meat, fish, or tofu is roughly 25-30 g. Three of those plus a yogurt or a shake gets you there.

sections.heading: Easy sources
items: A protein shake when you're short

sections.heading: The rule
sections.body: No meal counts as a meal unless it has a protein in it. Toast and coffee is not breakfast — add eggs or yogurt to it.

how_to.counts_as_done: Protein at all three meals today, roughly 140 g total.

steps.title: One plate, kitchen closed after dinner
steps.details: One plate per meal, no going back for seconds. After dinner, the kitchen is closed — no grazing, no snacks in front of the TV, no late-night cereal. Water, tea, or nothing until breakfast.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 1-2: one plate at dinner only. Weeks 3-4: one plate at every meal, kitchen closed every night.

how_to.gist: One plate per meal, and nothing to eat after dinner.
how_to.why: You never gave me a read on your eating, so we're not counting calories — we're changing two things that quietly add up: second helpings and evening grazing.

sections.heading: The plate rule
sections.body: Serve once, eat it, done. If you're still hungry twenty minutes later, have a glass of water first — real hunger survives that, habit hunger doesn't.

sections.heading: Closing the kitchen
sections.body: After dinner, the kitchen is shut. Brush your teeth right after you eat — it's a clean signal that the day's eating is over. Water and tea are fine.

sections.heading: The evening hour
sections.body: The grazing usually isn't hunger, it's boredom in front of a screen. Have something else ready for that slot — the walk, a shower, a book, a phone call.

how_to.counts_as_done: One plate at every meal and nothing eaten after dinner.

steps.title: In bed by 11pm
steps.details: Lights out by 11pm, aiming for 7-9 hours of sleep. Set an alarm for 30 minutes before bed — that's your cue to stop what you're doing, brush your teeth, and get in. Phone charges in another room.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 1-2: be in bed by 11:30pm. Weeks 3-4: 11pm, and keep the wake time fixed even on weekends.

how_to.gist: Lights out by 11pm, phone charging in another room.
how_to.why: Short sleep makes you hungrier the next day and makes the gym feel heavier. It's the one thing in this plan that quietly decides whether the other five hold.

sections.heading: The routine
items: 10:30pm: alarm goes off — stop what you're doing
Brush your teeth, kitchen stays shut
Phone goes on the charger in another room

sections.heading: Why the phone leaves
sections.body: Scrolling in bed is what turns an 11pm bedtime into midnight. If it's in another room, getting up to fetch it is more effort than going to sleep.

sections.heading: The wake time
sections.body: Pick a wake time and hold it every day, weekends included. A fixed wake time is what makes an earlier bedtime actually stick — lying in on Saturday undoes the whole week.

how_to.counts_as_done: Lights out by 11pm, phone in another room.

steps.title: Weigh in once a week
steps.details: Saturday morning, after the bathroom, before eating or drinking, same scale, same spot. Write the number down. One weigh-in a week — daily weighing will just make you crazy over water weight.
steps.week_progression: Same every week. Look at the four-week trend, never a single Saturday.

how_to.gist: One weigh-in a week, Saturday morning, same scale, written down.
how_to.why: You need to know whether this is working, and you need it without the daily noise of water weight. One number a week tells you the trend; seven numbers a week tells you nothing but mood.

sections.heading: The routine
items: Same scale, same spot on the floor

sections.heading: Reading it
sections.body: Single weeks bounce around — a salty dinner can add a kilo overnight. Only the four-week direction means anything. If it's flat or down over a month, the plan is working.

sections.heading: If it stalls
sections.body: Two flat weeks in a row is the signal to tighten one rule, not to panic. Cut the evening snack, or add 10 minutes to the walk.

how_to.counts_as_done: This Saturday's number written down.

phases.title: Longer walks, heavier lifts
phases.focus: The walk grows to 40 minutes and the gym weights start climbing. Meals stay the same three rules — they're working, so don't touch them. Bedtime holds at 11pm.

steps.title: Walk 40 minutes
steps.details: The daily walk grows to 40 minutes. Same conversational pace. If 40 minutes in one go doesn't fit the day, split it into 20 and 20.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 5-6: 35 minutes. Weeks 7-8: 40 minutes.

how_to.gist: 40 minutes of walking a day, split into two blocks if that's what fits.
how_to.why: The walk is your biggest daily lever and it's already a habit by now — this is the cheapest place to add effort, because it costs you nothing new to learn.

sections.heading: Building up
sections.body: Go to 35 minutes for two weeks, then 40. Don't jump straight to 40 — the point is that it stays easy enough to do every single day.

sections.heading: If it doesn't fit
sections.body: Two 20-minute blocks count. One before work, one after dinner is the easiest split.

how_to.counts_as_done: 40 minutes of walking done today, in one block or two.

steps.title: Gym session — full body, heavier
steps.details: Same four moves, same two days, 3 sets of 8-12. The weights should be noticeably heavier than week one by now — you're adding 2.5 kg / 5 lbs to your main lift whenever you hit the top of the rep range.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 5-8: 3 sets of 8-12, adding weight whenever you hit 12 reps on all sets.

how_to.gist: Same two sessions, same four moves — the weights go up.
how_to.why: This is where the muscle-keeping actually happens. Two sessions a week only works if the numbers on the bar keep moving.

sections.heading: The rule
sections.body: Hit 12 reps on all three sets of an exercise? Add 2.5 kg / 5 lbs next session and drop back to 8. That's the whole progression.

sections.heading: If you stall
sections.body: Two sessions stuck at the same weight is normal. Hold it and add a rep. Three sessions stuck, drop 10% and build back up — you'll pass it.

how_to.counts_as_done: Both sessions done this week.

steps.title: Write down every set and beat last time
steps.details: Keep logging every working set, and keep beating one number from last session. By now the log should show a clear upward line on your main lift from week one.
steps.week_progression: Same habit, higher numbers. If the log is flat for three sessions, drop the weight 10% and rebuild.

how_to.gist: Log every set, beat one number from last session.
how_to.why: The log is the only honest record of whether the gym days are doing anything. Without it you'll repeat the same weights for three months and wonder why nothing changed.

sections.heading: Before you start
sections.body: Open last session's numbers and pick one to beat. One rep, or 2.5 kg / 5 lbs on your main lift.

sections.heading: If it's flat
sections.body: Three sessions with no movement means the weight is too heavy to progress from. Drop 10% and build back up — you'll pass your old number within a few weeks.

how_to.counts_as_done: This session's sets written down, and one number from last time beaten.

steps.title: Protein at every meal
steps.details: Same 140 g target, now with a rough tally rather than a guess. Three palm-sized portions plus a yogurt or shake gets you there.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 5-8: hit 140 g most days, not just some.

how_to.gist: About 140 g of protein a day, tallied roughly.
how_to.why: Protein is what keeps the hunger down while you're eating less. It's the one number in this plan worth paying attention to.

sections.heading: The target
sections.body: 140 g a day. A palm of meat, fish, or tofu is 25-30 g. Three of those plus a yogurt or a shake and you're there.

sections.heading: The rule
sections.body: Every meal has a protein in it. If a meal doesn't, it's a snack — and snacks don't hold you until the next meal.

how_to.counts_as_done: Protein at all three meals today, roughly 140 g total.

steps.title: One plate, kitchen closed after dinner
steps.details: Same two rules, no changes. If the scale has been flat two weeks running, this is the rule to tighten first — smaller plate, or dinner finished an hour earlier.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 5-8: hold the rules. Tighten only if the four-week trend is flat.

how_to.gist: One plate per meal, nothing after dinner.
how_to.why: These two rules are doing the calorie work without any counting. They only stop working if you stop doing them.

sections.heading: If the scale stalls
sections.body: Two flat weeks means tighten one thing, not everything. Smaller dinner plate, or kitchen closed an hour earlier. Change one, hold it two weeks, then look again.

sections.heading: The evening
sections.body: Teeth brushed after dinner, kitchen shut. Water and tea only.

how_to.counts_as_done: One plate at every meal and nothing eaten after dinner.

steps.title: In bed by 11pm
steps.details: Same 11pm lights-out, same fixed wake time. If you've been sliding later, this is the first thing to pull back — short sleep shows up as hunger and skipped walks.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 5-8: hold 11pm. If you've drifted past midnight, pull it back 15 minutes a week until it's 11 again.

how_to.gist: Lights out by 11pm, same wake time every day.
how_to.why: By week five the walks are longer and the weights are heavier — both of those get harder on short sleep, and harder still to keep doing.

sections.heading: If you've drifted
sections.body: Don't jump from midnight to 11pm in one night. Move bedtime 15 minutes earlier each week until you're back at 11, and keep the wake time fixed the whole time.

sections.heading: The signal
sections.body: 10:30pm alarm, teeth brushed, phone in another room. Same four steps every night.

how_to.counts_as_done: Lights out by 11pm, phone in another room.

steps.title: Weigh in once a week
steps.details: Same Saturday routine. By now you should have eight numbers and a direction. Read the trend, not the week.
steps.week_progression: Same every week.

phases.title: Hold the line and finish it
phases.focus: Nothing new gets added — the walk, the two sessions, the three meal rules and the 11pm bedtime carry you to the finish. This phase is about not getting bored and not drifting.

steps.title: Walk 40 minutes
steps.details: Hold 40 minutes a day. Same pace, same rain plan. If you've been walking the same route for three months, change it — boredom is what kills this, not difficulty.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 9-12: hold at 40 minutes.

how_to.gist: 40 minutes a day, held steady to the finish.
how_to.why: The last month is where people quietly stop. The walk is the habit most likely to drift, because it's the one that feels optional.

sections.heading: Keep it interesting
sections.body: Same route for three months gets skipped. Change the route, add a podcast you only listen to while walking, walk somewhere with a destination.

sections.heading: If you miss
sections.body: One day off is fine. Two in a row is the start of the end — walk the next day no matter what.

how_to.counts_as_done: 40 minutes of walking done today, in one block or two.

steps.title: Gym session — full body, heaviest yet
steps.details: Same two sessions, same four moves, 3 sets of 8-12. Your main lift should be meaningfully heavier than week one. Keep adding 2.5 kg / 5 lbs whenever you hit 12 reps on all sets.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 9-12: keep progressing. If you've stalled three sessions, drop 10% and rebuild.

how_to.gist: Two sessions a week, still adding weight to the bar.
how_to.why: You're in the last month of a cut — this is exactly when the body starts eyeing your muscle. The lifting is what tells it no.

sections.heading: The rule
sections.body: 12 reps on all three sets? Add 2.5 kg / 5 lbs next time. That's it.

sections.heading: If you stall
sections.body: Three sessions stuck, drop 10% and build back. You'll pass the old number in a few weeks.

how_to.counts_as_done: Both sessions done this week.

steps.title: Write down every set and beat last time
steps.details: Keep the log going to the last session. Twelve weeks of numbers is proof of what you did — and the starting point if you want to keep going.
steps.week_progression: Same habit, right through week 12.

steps.title: Protein at every meal
steps.details: Same 140 g target. Hold it to the end — the last four weeks are when people loosen up and give back what they earned.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 9-12: hold 140 g.

steps.title: One plate, kitchen closed after dinner
steps.details: Same two rules to the end. If the four-week trend has been flat, tighten one: smaller plate, or dinner an hour earlier.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 9-12: hold the rules. Tighten one only if the trend is flat.

how_to.gist: One plate per meal, nothing after dinner, to week 12.
how_to.why: These are the rules doing the actual fat loss. They're boring, which is exactly why they work.

sections.heading: If the trend is flat
sections.body: Change one thing only — smaller dinner plate, or kitchen closed an hour earlier. Hold it two weeks before judging.

sections.heading: The evening
sections.body: Teeth brushed after dinner, kitchen shut, water and tea only.

how_to.counts_as_done: One plate at every meal and nothing eaten after dinner.

steps.title: In bed by 11pm
steps.details: Same 11pm lights-out to the end. The last month is when late nights creep back in — hold the bedtime and the fixed wake time.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 9-12: hold 11pm, fixed wake time.

steps.title: Weigh in once a week
steps.details: Same Saturday weigh-in. Twelve numbers by the end — enough to see the whole story rather than any single week of it.
steps.week_progression: Same every week.

milestones.title: Four weeks of walks, gym days and 11pm bedtimes
milestones.criteria: You've walked most days, hit both gym sessions every week, and been in bed by 11pm most nights for four weeks, and the Saturday numbers are written down. The scale may only have moved a little — that's expected at this stage.

milestones.title: Eight weeks in, and the bar is heavier
milestones.criteria: Your main lift is noticeably heavier than week one and the log shows it. The walk is at 40 minutes. The four-week weight trend is heading down.

milestones.title: Ten pounds down, habits intact
milestones.criteria: Twelve weeks of walks, two gym sessions a week, the three meal rules and the 11pm bedtime held. The four-week weight trend is down and your main lift is heavier than when you started.

protocol.coach_notes: Ten pounds in twelve weeks is about a pound a week — the version of this that actually survives a bad weekend, a work trip, and a rainy Tuesday. Nothing here is heroic: a walk you already had room for, two gym days you already said you'd do, three meal rules you can check off without counting a single calorie, and a bedtime that keeps the rest of it running. The one thing that decides this is what happens after a miss — one skipped day is noise, the day after it is the whole habit. Do the rep after the miss and this lands.

sessions.goal: I want to gain 5 lbs of lean muscle.

protocol.goal_statement: Get to bed by 11pm on weeknights for a month — lights out, phone out of the bedroom, show off by 10:30.

phases.title: Move the phone, stop the show
phases.focus: Get the phone out of the bedroom and put a fixed end time on the show — the two things that actually decide when you fall asleep.

steps.title: Charge your phone in the kitchen overnight
steps.details: From night one, the phone charges in the kitchen, not next to the pillow. Plug it in when you start winding down and leave it there until morning. If you use it as an alarm, pick up a cheap alarm clock or set the kitchen one — that's the whole reason it's been living by your bed.

how_to.gist: Phone charges in the kitchen from wind-down until morning — every weeknight.
how_to.why: Scrolling in bed is the last thing standing between you and sleep, and it's the one thing you've never had to resist because the phone is always within arm's reach. Take the option away and 11pm stops being a decision you have to win.

sections.heading: The move
sections.body: When you start winding down, walk the phone to the kitchen and plug it in there. It stays there until your alarm goes off in the morning. Not on the nightstand, not on the floor beside the bed — the kitchen.

sections.heading: The alarm problem
items: Get a cheap alarm clock, or set an alarm on a kitchen device
If you truly need the phone as a backup alarm, set it before you walk it out
No 'just checking one thing' trips back to the kitchen after lights out

sections.heading: If you slip
sections.body: If the phone ends up in the bedroom, don't write off the night — walk it back out and get in bed. One night of scrolling doesn't undo the week; two in a row starts to.

how_to.counts_as_done: Phone spent the night in the kitchen, and you didn't bring it back to the bedroom after lights out.

steps.week_progression: Every weeknight this week. If you're up later than usual, the phone still goes to the kitchen — that part doesn't move.

steps.title: Show off by 10:30
steps.details: Pick the episode before you sit down, and when it ends, the TV goes off — no 'one more'. If you're mid-episode at 10:30, that's the end of the night's watching. The show has no natural stopping point, so you're giving it one.

how_to.gist: TV off by 10:30 — episode picked in advance, no 'one more'.
how_to.why: A show with no end time always wins the 10:45 argument, because at 10:45 the decision is still open. Give it a fixed stop and there's nothing left to negotiate.

sections.heading: Before you sit down
sections.body: Choose the episode before you press play, so you know exactly where the night ends. If the episode runs past 10:30, start it earlier or pick a shorter one — the stop time doesn't move.

sections.heading: At 10:30

steps.week_progression: Week 4: two-sentence answers. Week 5: three-question exchanges. Week 6: a full minute on one topic without stopping.

steps.title: Two Spanish-only sessions with your partner
steps.details: The Saturday session stays, and a short Wednesday evening one joins it — 15 minutes, Spanish only. Two live sessions a week is where the back-and-forth actually starts to feel normal instead of terrifying.
steps.week_progression: Week 4: 15 minutes each. Week 5: 20 minutes each. Week 6: Saturday runs 25 minutes without a break.

steps.title: Review the week's material out loud
steps.details: First five minutes of each morning: everything from the last three days, out loud, from memory. Three days back, not one — that's what moves words from 'I just learned this' to 'I can use this'.
steps.week_progression: Week 4: two days back. Week 5: three days back. Week 6: three days back plus last Saturday's gaps.

steps.title: Pick one topic and prepare it properly
steps.details: Each week choose one topic you'd actually want to talk about — your job, your family, food, last weekend — and build the ten sentences you'd need for it. Then use it in the partner session. By week six you should have six topics you can hold for a minute each.
steps.week_progression: Week 4: two topics. Week 5: four. Week 6: six, each rehearsed out loud.

steps.title: Listen to Spanish for ten minutes a day
steps.details: Ten minutes of Spanish audio you can mostly follow — a slow-news podcast, a learner series, a show with Spanish subtitles. Not background noise: you're listening for words you know, and you stop and rewind when you catch one you don't.
steps.week_progression: Week 4: slow learner audio. Week 5: slow news. Week 6: a show with Spanish subtitles on.

phases.title: Five minutes without stopping
phases.focus: Build the stamina to keep a conversation going for the full five minutes, including when you get stuck.

steps.title: 30 minutes of Spanish before work
steps.details: Same slot. Now the mornings are mostly speaking — you talk out loud to yourself about your day, your plans, what you're making for dinner, for ten minutes straight, then review the words you stumbled on.
steps.week_progression: Week 7: 5 minutes talking without stopping. Week 8: 8 minutes. Week 9: 10 minutes.

steps.title: Two Spanish-only sessions with your partner
steps.details: Wednesday 20 minutes, Saturday 30 minutes, Spanish only. From week seven, Saturday includes one unbroken five-minute stretch where she keeps the conversation going and you don't stop, even when you're fumbling.
steps.week_progression: Week 7: 3-minute unbroken stretch. Week 8: 4 minutes. Week 9: the full 5 minutes.

steps.title: Practise getting unstuck
steps.details: In each partner session, deliberately hit a wall: talk about something you have no vocabulary for. Then use the escape phrases — '¿Cómo se dice...?', 'No entiendo', 'Más despacio, por favor' — instead of switching to English. Getting stuck is not failure; getting stuck and going silent is what ends a conversation.
steps.week_progression: Week 7: use one escape phrase per session. Week 8: two. Week 9: keep the conversation alive for a full minute after getting stuck.

steps.title: Review the week's material out loud
steps.details: First five minutes each morning, out loud, from memory — now covering the whole week's material, not just the last few days. This is the part that makes the words permanent.
steps.week_progression: Week 7: four days back. Week 8: five days. Week 9: the whole week plus the escape phrases.

steps.title: Listen to Spanish for fifteen minutes a day
steps.details: Fifteen minutes of Spanish audio, subtitles off for the first pass. You're training your ear for the speed real people speak at — which is faster than anything you've been listening to so far.
steps.week_progression: Week 7: subtitles on. Week 8: subtitles off for the first listen, on for the second. Week 9: subtitles off throughout.

phases.title: Five minutes, for real
phases.focus: Rehearse and then hold the actual five-minute conversation, with someone other than your partner.

steps.title: 30 minutes of Spanish before work
steps.details: Same slot, and now the mornings are rehearsal: run the five-minute conversation out loud, start to finish, twice. Same opening, same topics, until the first thirty seconds are automatic and you can spend your attention on what comes next.
steps.week_progression: Week 10: rehearse the opening. Week 11: rehearse the full five minutes twice. Week 12: rehearse once, then improvise a new topic.

steps.title: Two Spanish-only sessions with your partner
steps.details: Wednesday 20 minutes, Saturday 30 minutes. From week ten, your partner stops being helpful: no slowing down unless you ask, no finishing your sentences, no switching to English when you struggle. She's now playing a stranger, not a coach.
steps.week_progression: Week 10: she stops finishing your sentences. Week 11: she speaks at normal speed. Week 12: she starts topics you haven't prepared.

steps.title: Have a five-minute conversation with someone new
steps.details: Once in these three weeks — ideally in week eleven or twelve — have a five-minute conversation in Spanish with someone who isn't your partner. A colleague, a neighbour, a shopkeeper, a tutor on a call. This is the real test: your partner knows your patterns and fills your gaps without meaning to.
steps.week_progression: Week 10: line someone up. Week 11: do it, even if it's four minutes. Week 12: do it again, or extend to the full five.

steps.title: Review the week's material out loud
steps.details: First five minutes each morning, out loud, from memory. By now this should be fast — if it's taking longer than five minutes, you're reviewing too much and should cut back to the phrases you actually use.
steps.week_progression: Week 10: full week. Week 11: full week plus the new person's vocabulary. Week 12: full week, then stop and just talk.

steps.title: Listen to Spanish for fifteen minutes a day
steps.details: Fifteen minutes, subtitles off, at normal speed. Pick something you'd genuinely want to watch — the point is that by week twelve this is something you do because you like it, not because it's on the list.
steps.week_progression: Week 10: normal-speed audio, subtitles off. Week 11: a show you actually enjoy. Week 12: keep it going past the plan.

milestones.title: Three weeks of mornings, unbroken
milestones.criteria: You've done the 30-minute morning session five days a week for three straight weeks, and you've had three Spanish-only sessions with your partner. You can introduce yourself, say where you live, and say what you did today — out loud, without reading.

milestones.title: A full minute, no English
milestones.criteria: You can talk about one topic for a full minute in Spanish without switching to English, and you've got six prepared topics you can hold. Your partner sessions are running 20-25 minutes.

milestones.title: Five minutes without stopping
milestones.criteria: In a partner session you held an unbroken five-minute stretch of Spanish, including at least one moment where you got stuck and used a phrase to get yourself out instead of going quiet.

milestones.title: Five minutes with someone new
milestones.criteria: You had a five-minute conversation in Spanish with someone who isn't your partner — and it worked. Twelve weeks ago you knew twenty words.

protocol.coach_notes: Weeks two through four are the danger zone: you'll feel like nothing is sticking, and that feeling is completely normal rather than a sign this isn't working. The mornings are the whole plan, so protect them on the days you least want to — one missed morning is noise, two in a row is how this dies. Your partner is the unfair advantage here; most people trying this have nobody to talk to, so use her early and often, and let her be unhelpful on purpose in the last few weeks.
