protocol.goal_statement: Read 10 pages in bed at 10:30 on weeknights, phone charging in the kitchen overnight, plus one audiobook chapter on the Saturday walk
protocol.short_title: Read 10 pages a night on weeknights

phases.title: Set the trap
phases.focus: Get the phone out of the bedroom and the book in your hands at 10:30 — ten pages, every weeknight, with a two-page floor for the nights that go sideways.

steps.title: Phone charges in the kitchen overnight
steps.details: Every night, the phone goes on the kitchen charger and stays there until morning. This is the one that does the work — the thing that's been beating you at 10:30 just isn't in the room. Set the charger up tonight, before you need it.

how_to.gist: Phone on the kitchen charger before bed, every night, no exceptions.
how_to.why: You told me the phone is what pulls you off the page. Moving it out of the bedroom means you're not fighting it at 10:30pm — it's simply not there.

sections.heading: The setup
sections.body: Put a charger in the kitchen and leave it plugged in there permanently. Tonight, before bed, walk the phone out and plug it in. That's the whole move.

sections.heading: The rule
sections.body: Once the phone is on the kitchen charger, it stays there until morning. No bringing it back to bed for an alarm, a last scroll, or a quick check. If you use your phone as an alarm, get a cheap clock or set an alarm on something else this week.

sections.heading: If you slip
sections.body: If the phone ends up in the bedroom, plug it in the kitchen the next night anyway. One night back in the room doesn't undo the setup — it just means you run it again tomorrow.

how_to.counts_as_done: The phone spent the night on the kitchen charger.

steps.week_progression: Weeks 1-4: every night, including weekends. The charger lives in the kitchen from night one.

steps.title: Read 10 pages in bed at 10:30
steps.details: Weeknights, in bed, at 10:30 — book open, ten pages. The book lives on your pillow or your nightstand during the day so it's the first thing your hand finds. Ten pages is small enough to finish tired, which is the point.

how_to.gist: In bed at 10:30 on weeknights, ten pages of the book, then lights out.
how_to.why: Ten pages is a target you can hit on a bad night, which is the only kind of target that lasts. Doing it in bed at a fixed time means you're not deciding whether to read — you're just already there.

sections.heading: The setup
sections.body: Keep the book you're reading on your pillow or nightstand during the day, so it's the first thing your hand lands on when you get into bed. Have the next book ready before you finish the current one.

sections.heading: The night
items: Phone goes to the kitchen charger

sections.heading: The floor
sections.body: On nights work blows up and ten pages isn't happening, two pages counts. Two pages keeps the week alive. What doesn't count is zero — and never two zeros in a row.

how_to.counts_as_done: Ten pages read in bed on a weeknight (two pages on a brutal night).

steps.week_progression: Weeks 1-2: ten pages, and two pages is a fully legitimate night. Weeks 3-4: same ten pages, but the two-page floor should be getting rare.

steps.title: One audiobook chapter on the Saturday walk
steps.details: Saturday, on your walk, headphones in and one chapter of an audiobook. This is your second channel — it keeps the week alive on weeks the weeknights fall apart. Have the audiobook downloaded and queued before Saturday so there's no fumbling at the door.

how_to.gist: Saturday walk, one audiobook chapter, headphones in from the first step.
how_to.why: This is the backup that busy weeks can't kill. If the weeknights collapse, this one chapter still means the week wasn't a write-off.

sections.heading: Before Saturday
sections.body: Download the audiobook and queue up the next chapter during the week, so on Saturday you just press play. Pick something you actually want to hear — this one should feel like a treat, not homework.

sections.heading: The walk
sections.body: Start the chapter as you head out the door. One chapter is the target; if it runs long and you keep listening, that's a bonus, not a requirement.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.body: Last year the routine died when work got busy. This is the piece that survives a busy week — one walk, one chapter, week still live.

how_to.counts_as_done: One audiobook chapter finished on the Saturday walk.

steps.week_progression: Weeks 1-4: one chapter every Saturday. Same walk, same slot.

steps.title: Never let two weeknights go by with zero pages
steps.details: Your last attempt died in week two when work got busy — this is the answer to that night. If you miss a weeknight, the very next weeknight you read at least two pages, even if it's 11:30 and you're wrecked. One missed night is noise. Two in a row is how the whole thing ends.

how_to.gist: After any missed weeknight, the next weeknight gets at least two pages.
how_to.why: This is the one thing your plan was missing. Last year the reading goal died in week two when work got busy — not because you missed a night, but because you missed a few and never came back. This rule is the coming-back.

sections.heading: The rule
sections.body: Miss a weeknight? The next weeknight, you read at least two pages. Not ten, not the missed pages made up — two. The point is that the chain restarts immediately, while it's still cheap.

sections.heading: The bad week
sections.body: If work eats three nights in a row, you don't owe anyone the missed pages. You owe two pages on the next weeknight you're home. A bad week stays a bad week instead of becoming a quit.

sections.heading: The backup
sections.body: If the whole weeknight stretch collapses, the Saturday audiobook chapter still counts as a live week. You're never at zero.

how_to.counts_as_done: No two weeknights in a row with zero pages read.

steps.week_progression: Weeks 1-4: this is the rule that gets tested. Expect it to come up at least once.

phases.title: Make it the default
phases.focus: Ten pages stops being a decision and starts being what happens at 10:30. The book is always waiting, the phone is always in the kitchen.

steps.title: Phone charges in the kitchen overnight
steps.details: Same as before — phone on the kitchen charger every night. By now this should feel like part of the house rather than a rule you're following.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 5-8: unchanged. If you've been carrying the phone back to bed on weekends, this is where the weekend nights get locked in too.

steps.title: Read 10 pages in bed at 10:30
steps.details: Weeknights, in bed, 10:30, ten pages. Same target — the change is that the two-page floor should now be rare rather than routine. If you find yourself reaching for it most weeks, that's information, not failure.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 5-8: ten pages, with the floor used rarely. If ten feels easy most nights, you may read on past it — that's fine, the target stays ten.

steps.title: One audiobook chapter on the Saturday walk
steps.details: Saturday walk, one chapter. Keep the queue stocked during the week so you never start Saturday with nothing downloaded.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 5-8: one chapter. If you've been finishing the chapter and stopping mid-walk, let it run — the walk is yours.

steps.title: Never let two weeknights go by with zero pages
steps.details: The same rule, still standing. After any missed weeknight, the next one gets at least two pages. This is the piece that keeps a busy week from becoming the end of the routine.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 5-8: unchanged. It should be coming up less often now — that's the sign it's working.

steps.title: Start the next book before you finish the current one
steps.details: Added because the gap between books is where reading routines quietly die — you finish something, nothing's waiting, and three weeks pass. Keep one book queued up so the night after you finish, there's already something on the nightstand.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 5-8: whenever you're within about 50 pages of the end, line up the next one.

phases.title: Read past the target
phases.focus: The routine holds on its own now. This phase adds a little room to read more on the nights you want to, without turning ten pages into a bigger obligation.

steps.title: Phone charges in the kitchen overnight
steps.details: Phone on the kitchen charger every night. By week nine this should be the least interesting part of the plan, which is exactly what you want.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 9-12: unchanged.

steps.title: Read 10 pages in bed at 10:30
steps.details: Ten pages, weeknights, in bed at 10:30. The target doesn't move — what changes is that on the nights the book has you, you stay in it. Ten is the floor you never negotiate; anything past it is a good night, not a new standard.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 9-12: ten pages as the standing target. Read on past it whenever you want to — no pressure to make that the new normal.

steps.title: One audiobook chapter on the Saturday walk
steps.details: Saturday walk, one chapter. If you've got a book you're excited about, this is the slot to let it run long.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 9-12: one chapter minimum. Let it run if you're into it.

steps.title: Never let two weeknights go by with zero pages
steps.details: Still the rule. After a missed weeknight, the next one gets two pages. This is what you carry out of the twelve weeks — the routine can survive a bad week, which is the thing last year's attempt couldn't do.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 9-12: unchanged. This one stays after the plan ends.

steps.title: Start the next book before you finish the current one
steps.details: Keep a book queued so there's never a gap between finishing one and starting the next. This is the habit that keeps the whole thing running after week twelve.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 9-12: same — always something waiting on the nightstand.

milestones.title: Four weeks in — the phone's been sleeping in the kitchen
milestones.criteria: The phone charged in the kitchen nearly every night for four weeks, and you read on most weeknights. The Saturday chapter happened every week.

milestones.title: You survived a busy week without quitting
milestones.criteria: At least one week where work blew up and you still came back to the book the next weeknight instead of letting it go. This is the thing that killed last year's attempt.

milestones.title: Bedtime with a book is just what happens now
milestones.criteria: Eight weeks of weeknight reading, with the two-page floor used rarely rather than routinely. The book is on the nightstand without you thinking about it.

milestones.title: Twelve weeks, and the shelf is finally getting shorter
milestones.criteria: The routine held for the full twelve weeks — weeknights in bed, phone in the kitchen, Saturday chapter — through at least one bad week. You're reading most nights without deciding to.

protocol.coach_notes: You wrote this plan yourself, and that's most of why it'll work — you already knew the phone was the problem and moved it out of the room instead of promising to resist it. The only thing I added is the floor: two pages on the nights work blows up, and never two zeros in a row. That single rule is the difference between last year's week-two ending and a routine that survives a bad stretch. One missed night is noise. The night after a miss is the one that decides this, so make it two pages and move on.

sessions.goal: Lose 10 lbs

protocol.goal_statement: Lose 10 lbs (about 4.5 kg) — roughly 1 lb a week via a small daily calorie deficit, two gym sessions a week, and a daily walk.

phases.title: Set the rules
phases.focus: Two lifts, a daily walk, three food rules you can actually keep, a protein number, and a bedtime — plus the first real weight numbers this plan has ever had.

steps.title: Lift twice a week
steps.details: Two full-body sessions, Tuesday and Saturday. Squat or leg press, a push, a pull, a hinge, and a carry — three sets of 8-10 each, stopping a rep or two short of failure. 2-3 light warm-up sets before your first working set on each lift. Rest days are rest days.

how_to.gist: Two full-body sessions, Tue and Sat, 3 sets of 8-10 per lift.
how_to.why: This is the muscle-insurance policy. Lose 10 lbs without lifting and a chunk of it comes off muscle, which is why so many people end up lighter and softer. Two sessions a week is enough to hold what you've got.

sections.heading: The week
items: Any other day — no lifting, just the walk

sections.heading: The session
sections.body: Pick one movement per pattern: squat or leg press, a press, a row or pulldown, a hinge (deadlift or hip thrust), and a carry or plank. Three sets of 8-10 reps each. Start lighter than you think — week one is about showing up twice, not about numbers.

sections.heading: How hard
sections.body: Stop each set when you could still grind out one or two more reps. That's the sweet spot for keeping muscle while you're eating less. Grinding to failure every set just makes you sore and tired.

how_to.counts_as_done: Two sessions done this week, any order, any time of day.

steps.week_progression: Weeks 1-3: same two sessions, same sets. Add a small amount of weight only when 10 reps feels comfortable.

steps.title: Walk every day
steps.details: Thirty minutes of walking, every day, at a pace where you could hold a conversation. One block or split into two — a 15-minute loop at lunch and 15 after dinner both count. Rain, cold, and busy days included; indoors counts.

how_to.gist: 30 minutes of walking a day, any time, any weather.
how_to.why: You already walk daily and sit at a desk the rest of the time. This keeps that habit protected and turns it into the second half of your daily burn, so the food side doesn't have to do all the work.

sections.heading: When
sections.body: Pick your slot now and put it in your calendar: lunch break, right after work, or after dinner. Same slot every day beats a perfect slot you never use.

sections.heading: The pace
sections.body: Brisk enough that you're breathing a little harder but could still talk in full sentences. If you're gasping, slow down. If you're strolling, speed up.

sections.heading: Bad days
sections.body: Tired, raining, late — do 15 minutes instead of 30 and count it. A short walk keeps the chain going; a skipped walk starts the drift.

how_to.counts_as_done: 30 minutes walked, or 15 on a rough day — the app shows the minutes.

steps.week_progression: Weeks 1-3: 30 minutes daily. If 30 already feels easy, keep it there — the walk is the floor, not the challenge.

steps.title: Hit 140 g protein a day
steps.details: Roughly 140 g of protein a day — a palm-sized portion at breakfast, lunch, and dinner, plus a shake or a tub of Greek yogurt to close the gap. At your weight that's the amount that keeps you full on less food and protects muscle while the scale moves.

how_to.gist: About 140 g of protein a day — a portion at each meal plus a shake.
how_to.why: Protein is what makes a smaller amount of food feel like enough, and it's what keeps the weight you lose coming off fat instead of muscle. At your size, 140 g is the number that does both.

sections.heading: The target

how_to.counts_as_done: Three protein portions plus a shake or yogurt — the app shows 140 g or more.

steps.week_progression: Weeks 1-3: get a protein portion into all three meals. Weeks 4+: the shake or yogurt becomes a daily habit, not just a hungry-day one.

steps.title: One plate, no seconds
steps.details: Serve one plate at dinner and don't go back for more. Eat slowly enough that you notice you're done. If you're still hungry twenty minutes later, have fruit or yogurt — not a second plate. This is the whole deficit: a slightly smaller dinner, every night.

how_to.gist: One plate at dinner, no seconds, wait 20 minutes before more.
how_to.why: You never told me how you eat, so I'm not going to hand you a calorie number I made up. Instead this is the smallest change that reliably creates a daily deficit — one plate instead of one and a half, every night.

sections.heading: The rule
sections.body: One plate. Fill half of it with vegetables or salad, a quarter with protein, a quarter with rice, potatoes, or bread. When the plate's empty, you're done eating for the night.

sections.heading: The 20-minute test
sections.body: Fullness takes about twenty minutes to arrive. If you're still genuinely hungry after that, eat something — fruit, yogurt, a handful of nuts. Just not a second plate of dinner.

sections.heading: Eating out
sections.body: Order what you want, eat until you're satisfied, stop. Takeout isn't banned — a second dinner at 10pm is.

how_to.counts_as_done: One plate at dinner, no second helping.

steps.week_progression: Weeks 1-3: one plate at dinner. Weeks 4+: apply the same rule to lunch if dinners have become easy.

steps.title: No eating after 9pm
steps.details: Kitchen closes at 9pm. After that, water, tea, or nothing. If you're genuinely hungry, that's a sign dinner was too small — make dinner bigger tomorrow rather than eating now. This kills the late-night snacking that quietly erases a day's deficit.

how_to.gist: Kitchen closed after 9pm — water or tea only.
how_to.why: Late-night eating is the most common place a good day gets undone, and it's the easiest thing to cut because you're not actually hungry — you're bored, or it's just what you do on the couch.

sections.heading: The cutoff
sections.body: 9pm. Whatever's left of dinner goes in the fridge and the kitchen light goes off. Brush your teeth right after — it's a surprisingly effective full stop.

sections.heading: If you're hungry
sections.body: Genuine hunger at 9:30 means dinner was too small. Note it, and make tomorrow's dinner bigger. Don't fix it with a snack tonight.

sections.heading: Drinks count
sections.body: Beer, wine, and sugary drinks after 9pm count as eating. Water, plain tea, or black coffee don't.

how_to.counts_as_done: Nothing eaten after 9pm.

steps.week_progression: Weeks 1-3: hold the 9pm line. Weeks 4+: if it's automatic, move it to 8:30pm.

steps.title: Lights out by 11pm
steps.details: In bed with the lights off by 11pm, aiming for 7-9 hours before your alarm. Set an alarm for 10:30pm labelled "start winding down" — screens off, kitchen already closed, tomorrow's gym bag by the door. Short sleep makes you hungrier and blunts recovery from the lifts, which is the last thing a cut needs.

how_to.gist: Lights out by 11pm — 7-9 hours before your alarm.
how_to.why: Sleep is the quiet pillar of this plan. Too little of it makes you hungrier the next day and slows how well you recover from lifting, so the same food rules feel harder and the scale moves slower.

sections.heading: Why the alarm
sections.body: You won't feel tired at 10:30 — that's the point. The alarm is what makes 11pm happen instead of midnight.

sections.heading: Rough nights
sections.body: A late night happens. Don't try to make it up by sleeping in — get up at your normal time and go to bed on time the next night.

how_to.counts_as_done: Lights off by 11pm.

steps.week_progression: Weeks 1-3: hit 11pm most nights. Weeks 4+: it should be automatic — if you're consistently in bed by 10:45, keep it there.

steps.title: Weigh in and average it
steps.details: Step on the scale every morning, first thing, after the bathroom, before eating or drinking. Log the number. At the end of the week, look at the average, not any single day — daily weight swings 1-2 kg on water alone. The weekly average is the only number that means anything.

how_to.gist: Weigh yourself every morning and log it; judge the week by the average.
how_to.why: This is the plan's only real feedback loop. Without it we're guessing whether the food rules are working — with it, we can adjust from your actual numbers after two weeks instead of my assumptions.

sections.heading: How
sections.body: Same scale, same time, every morning: after the bathroom, before food or drink, in as little as you sleep in. Log it in the app. It takes eight seconds.

sections.heading: What to ignore
sections.body: Any single day. A salty dinner, a hard workout, or a bad night's sleep can move the scale 1-2 kg overnight. The weekly average is the number that tells the truth.

sections.heading: What to expect
sections.body: Roughly 0.5 kg a week on average, and it won't arrive in a straight line. Some weeks nothing moves, then two weeks' worth shows up at once. That's normal.

how_to.counts_as_done: Seven mornings logged, and you know this week's average.

steps.week_progression: Weeks 1-3: build the habit of logging daily. Weeks 4+: compare weekly averages and adjust one food rule if the average hasn't moved in two weeks.

phases.title: Make it bite

steps.title: Lift twice a week, heavier
steps.details: Same two full-body sessions, same five patterns. Now the goal is progress: add a small amount of weight or one extra rep to your main lift every session, and write it down. Three sets of 8-10, still stopping a rep or two short of failure.

how_to.gist: Same two sessions — add weight or a rep to your main lift each time.
how_to.why: By week four the sessions are routine, which means they can start doing more. Getting stronger while you're eating less is the clearest sign the weight coming off is fat and not muscle.

sections.heading: The progression
sections.body: Pick one main lift per session. If you hit 10 reps on all three sets last time, add the smallest jump your gym allows — 2.5 kg on a bar, one notch on a machine. If you didn't, stay at the same weight and add a rep.

sections.heading: Write it down
sections.body: Every set, every session, in your phone. You can't beat last week if you don't know what last week was.

steps.title: Walk 40 minutes a day
steps.details: The daily walk goes from 30 to 40 minutes. Same pace, same slot, same rules — split it into two blocks if that's what makes it happen. On lifting days, walk before or after the session, not instead of it.

how_to.gist: Daily walk goes up to 40 minutes — same slot, same pace.
how_to.why: Ten extra minutes a day is about 300 extra minutes a month of easy movement. It widens the deficit without touching your food, which is the cheapest way to keep the scale moving.

sections.heading: The change
sections.body: Forty minutes instead of thirty. Add it to the front or the back of your usual walk — don't find a new time of day for it.

sections.heading: Lifting days
sections.body: Tuesday and Saturday you still walk. Do it before the gym as a warm-up or after as a cooldown, whichever you'll actually do.

sections.heading: If 40 is too much
sections.body: Stay at 30 and add five minutes a week until you're there. The walk should never be the thing that makes you quit.

how_to.counts_as_done: 40 minutes walked, or 20 on a rough day.

steps.week_progression: Weeks 4-7: 40 minutes daily. Weeks 8-10: hold at 40.

steps.title: Protein at every meal, plus a shake
steps.details: Same target as before — roughly 140 g of protein a day — but now the shake or tub of Greek yogurt is a daily habit rather than a hungry-day rescue. Three palm-sized portions plus one shake gets you there.

how_to.gist: 140 g of protein a day — three portions plus a daily shake.
how_to.why: The deficit is a little sharper now, and protein is what keeps you from feeling like you're on a diet. It's also the strongest lever you have for keeping muscle while the scale drops.

sections.heading: The add-on
sections.body: One shake or one yogurt every day, not just on hungry days. That's the only change from weeks 1-3.

sections.heading: Why now
sections.body: Weeks 1-3 were about building the habit. Now that it's automatic, the extra protein is what lets the deficit get slightly bigger without you feeling worse.

sections.heading: Keep it simple
sections.body: You're not weighing food. Three palm-sized portions plus one shake lands around 140 g at your size, which is where you want to be.

how_to.counts_as_done: 140 g or more of protein today — the app shows the number.

steps.week_progression: Weeks 4-7: shake every day. Weeks 8-10: same.

steps.title: One plate at lunch too
steps.details: The one-plate rule now applies to lunch as well as dinner. Same shape: half vegetables or salad, a quarter protein, a quarter starch. No second helping, no afternoon vending-machine run to top it up.

how_to.gist: One plate at lunch as well as dinner — no seconds, no vending machine.
how_to.why: Dinner has been handled for three weeks. Lunch is the other meal where portions quietly creep, especially at a desk, and it's the last easy place to find a deficit without feeling deprived.

sections.heading: The plate

sections.heading: The afternoon
sections.body: If you're hungry at 3pm, that's a protein problem, not a willpower problem — have a yogurt or a handful of nuts instead of whatever's in the machine.

sections.heading: Eating out
sections.body: Order normally, eat to satisfied, stop. The rule is about seconds, not about restaurants.

how_to.counts_as_done: One plate at both lunch and dinner.

steps.week_progression: Weeks 4-7: one plate at lunch and dinner. Weeks 8-10: hold.

steps.title: Weigh in and read the trend
steps.details: Keep logging every morning. Now compare this week's average to last week's, and to where you started. If the average hasn't moved in two straight weeks, change one thing: drop the 9pm cutoff to 8:30, or trim the starch portion at dinner. One change, then wait two weeks.

how_to.gist: Keep logging daily; compare weekly averages and adjust one thing if it stalls.
how_to.why: This is where the plan stops guessing. Two flat weeks isn't failure — it's information, and it tells us exactly which dial to turn instead of cutting everything at once.

sections.heading: The read
sections.body: Every Sunday, write down the week's average. Compare it to last Sunday's. A drop of 0.3-0.7 kg is right on track.

sections.heading: If it stalls
sections.body: Two flat weeks in a row: change exactly one thing — the 9pm cutoff moves to 8:30, or dinner's starch portion gets smaller. Then wait two more weeks before changing anything else.

sections.heading: If it's dropping fast
sections.body: More than 1 kg a week for two weeks running means you're losing faster than you need to. Eat a bit more at dinner. This is a 10-week plan, not a race.

how_to.counts_as_done: Seven mornings logged and this week's average written down.

steps.week_progression: Weeks 4-7: weekly average compared week to week. Adjust one food rule only after two flat weeks.

phases.title: Land it
phases.focus: The last stretch: hold everything steady, keep the lifts heavy, and finish the ten weeks without a crash.

steps.title: Lift twice a week, hold the weights
steps.details: Same two sessions. The goal now is to hold your numbers, not chase new ones — eating less for ten weeks makes new personal bests unlikely, and that's fine. Keep the same weights and reps you finished week seven with, and keep writing them down.

how_to.gist: Same two sessions — hold your weights and keep logging them.
how_to.why: The end of a cut is when people quietly stop lifting, and that's exactly when muscle is most at risk. Holding your numbers for three more weeks is the whole job.

sections.heading: The goal
sections.body: Match last session's weights and reps. That's a win. If a lift feels genuinely easy, add a small jump — but don't chase it.

sections.heading: If you feel flat
sections.body: Being a little tired at the end of a cut is normal. Shorten the session if you need to — drop to two sets instead of three — but don't skip it.

how_to.counts_as_done: Two sessions done and logged.

steps.week_progression: Weeks 8-10: hold weights and reps steady. No new progression targets.

steps.title: Walk 40 minutes a day
steps.details: Hold the 40-minute daily walk through the finish. No increases — this is the level that got you here and it's the level that carries you across the line.

how_to.gist: Hold the 40-minute daily walk through week ten.
how_to.why: The walk is the part of this plan most likely to quietly disappear in the last few weeks, when the finish line is close and motivation dips. Holding it is what protects the deficit.

sections.heading: The rule
sections.body: Forty minutes, every day, same slot. Nothing changes for the last three weeks.

sections.heading: Rough days

how_to.counts_as_done: 40 minutes walked, or 15 on a rough day.

steps.week_progression: Weeks 8-10: hold at 40 minutes.

steps.title: Keep the three food rules
steps.details: Protein at every meal, one plate at lunch and dinner, nothing after 9pm. All three, every day, through week ten. No tightening, no new rules — the plan that got you here is the plan that finishes it.

how_to.gist: Protein at every meal, one plate at lunch and dinner, nothing after 9pm.
how_to.why: These three rules are the entire deficit. They've been working for seven weeks; the only job left is not to abandon them in the last stretch because the finish line is in sight.

sections.heading: One bad day

how_to.counts_as_done: All three rules held today.

steps.week_progression: Weeks 8-10: hold all three rules unchanged.

steps.title: Weigh in and finish the trend
steps.details: Keep logging every morning to the end. In week ten, compare your final weekly average to your starting average — that's your real result, not any single morning's number. Then decide what to hold: the walk and the lifts are worth keeping permanently.

how_to.gist: Log daily to the end; compare your final weekly average to where you started.
how_to.why: The trend line is the story of these ten weeks — the daily numbers are just noise. Seeing the whole line at the end is what makes the result feel real, and it tells you which habits are worth keeping.

sections.heading: The finish
sections.body: Week ten, compare your final weekly average to your week-one average. That difference is your result.

sections.heading: What to keep

sections.heading: If you're not quite there

protocol.coach_notes: Ten pounds at your size is a small ask, which is exactly why this plan is boring on purpose — two lifts, a walk, three food rules, a protein number, and a scale you read weekly instead of daily. The food side is the whole game here, and since you never told me how you eat, I built it from rules you can check off rather than a calorie number I'd have had to invent. Sleep is in there for a reason: short nights make the same rules feel twice as hard. One missed day is noise; the day after a miss is the one that decides this, so never miss twice.

sessions.goal: I want to lose 8 kg steadily over the next 4 months.

protocol.goal_statement: Lose 8 kg over 16 weeks — about 0.5 kg a week — by holding a modest daily calorie deficit, cooking at home as you already do, walking daily, and lifting twice a week to keep muscle.

steps.title: Lift twice a week
steps.details: Two full-body sessions, Tuesday and Saturday. Squat or leg press, a press, a row or pulldown, a hinge, then one arm and one core movement. 3 sets of 8-12 reps each, stopping 1-2 reps short of failure. 2-3 light warm-up sets before your first working set. This is what keeps the weight you lose coming off as fat instead of muscle.

how_to.gist: Two full-body sessions, Tuesday and Saturday, 3 sets of 8-12 per lift.
how_to.why: At half a kilo a week, lifting is the difference between losing fat and losing muscle. Two sessions is the floor that holds your strength while the scale moves.

phases.focus: Same skeleton, sharper edges — heavier lifts, a longer walk, a real look at what's in the cooking, and the bedtime held.

steps.title: Lift twice a week, heavier
steps.details: Same two sessions, same movements, more weight. Working sets move to 3-4 sets of 6-10 reps, still stopping 1-2 reps short of failure. Add 2.5 kg to your main lift whenever you hit the top of the rep range on all sets.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 5-7: 3 sets of 6-10. Weeks 8-9: 4 sets on your two main lifts.

steps.title: Beat your log every session
steps.details: Same log, higher bar: every session should show one number better than last time — a rep or 2.5 kg. If two sessions in a row show nothing, that's your signal to eat a little more on training days, not to train harder.
steps.week_progression: Every session, weeks 5-9.

steps.title: Walk 40 minutes every day
steps.details: Ten minutes more than last phase, same conversational pace. If 40 minutes daily starts feeling like a chore, keep 30 on weekdays and take a longer 60-minute walk on Saturday or Sunday.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 5-6: 40 minutes daily. Weeks 7-9: 40 daily with one 60-minute weekend walk.

steps.title: One plate at dinner, and measure the oil
steps.details: The one-plate rule stays. Now measure the cooking oil and butter — a tablespoon per pan, not a pour. This is usually where 200-300 hidden calories a day live in an otherwise good home-cooked diet.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 5-9: oil measured at every cooked meal.

steps.title: Protein at every meal, 150 g a day
steps.details: Same target as before, now counted rather than eyeballed. Roughly 150 g of protein a day from the food you already eat — a palm at each meal plus a yogurt or a shake if you come up short.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 5-9: counted daily.

steps.title: In bed by 11pm
steps.details: Same bedtime, held through the phase where the deficit starts to bite. If you're waking before your alarm and feeling flat in the gym, the fix is an earlier night, not more coffee.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 5-9: lights out by 11, every night.

steps.title: Weigh in every Sunday morning
steps.details: Same Sunday routine. By now you should be seeing roughly half a kilo a week come off across the month. If four Sundays show nothing, cut the evening extras before you cut meals.
steps.week_progression: Every Sunday, weeks 5-9.

phases.title: Hold the line
phases.focus: The middle stretch where motivation thins — the plan gets simpler, not harder, and the rules carry you.

steps.title: Lift twice a week
steps.details: Same two sessions, same weights as phase 2 — this phase is about not losing ground, not about adding. Keep 3-4 sets of 6-10 and keep stopping 1-2 reps short of failure.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 10-13: hold the weights steady.

steps.title: Beat your log every session
steps.details: Keep the log going. In this stretch, matching last week's numbers is a win — you're in a deficit and holding strength is the goal. Only push for more if it comes easily.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 10-13: match or beat, both count.

steps.title: Walk 40 minutes every day
steps.details: Unchanged from phase 2. The walk is the habit most likely to quietly disappear when life gets busy — it's also the one that costs you the least to keep. Same route, same time of day.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 10-13: 40 minutes daily, no changes.

steps.title: One plate at dinner, oil measured
steps.details: Both rules stay exactly as they are. If you've had a heavier weekend, don't compensate with a skipped meal — just go back to one plate on Monday.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 10-13: unchanged.

steps.title: Protein at every meal, 150 g a day
steps.details: Unchanged. Protein is what keeps this phase from turning into hunger and a lost month. If you're eating out more, order the protein first and build the meal around it.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 10-13: 150 g daily.

steps.title: In bed by 11pm
steps.details: Unchanged. This is the phase where a run of short nights turns into a run of big dinners, so the bedtime is doing more work here than it did in week one.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 10-13: lights out by 11, every night.

steps.title: Weigh in every Sunday morning
steps.details: Same Sunday routine. Around this point the loss often slows for a week or two — that's normal, not failure. Judge by the month, not the week.
steps.week_progression: Every Sunday, weeks 10-13.

phases.title: Land it
phases.focus: Last stretch — finish the 8 kg, then learn to hold it at maintenance instead of sliding back.

steps.title: Lift twice a week
steps.details: Same two sessions. Keep the weights where they are — the last three weeks are about arriving at the finish with your strength intact, not squeezing out a personal best.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 14-16: hold steady.

steps.title: Beat your log every session
steps.details: Keep logging through the finish. The log is the thing you'll carry into maintenance — it's how you'll know if strength starts slipping after the deficit ends.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 14-16: keep the record going.

steps.title: Walk 40 minutes every day
steps.details: Unchanged. This is the habit that keeps the weight off after the plan ends — it's the one to protect hardest in the last three weeks.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 14-16: 40 minutes daily.

steps.title: Add back one plate at dinner
steps.details: Once you're at your target weight, stop running the deficit: go back to a normal second helping when you're genuinely hungry, and keep the measured oil. The goal from here is holding the new weight, not losing more.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 14-15: still one plate. Week 16: eat to appetite, keep the oil measured.

steps.title: Protein at every meal, 150 g a day
steps.details: Keep the protein target even after the deficit ends. It's the single habit that makes the new weight the stable one rather than a stop on the way back up.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 14-16: 150 g daily, permanently.

steps.title: In bed by 11pm
steps.details: Keep the bedtime through the finish and after it. Sleep is what keeps your appetite steady once the deficit is gone and the scale stops giving you feedback every week.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 14-16: lights out by 11, every night.

steps.title: Weigh in every Sunday morning
steps.details: Keep the Sunday weigh-in going after the plan ends. A two-kilo drift caught in a month is a two-week fix; caught in six months it's the whole job again.
steps.week_progression: Every Sunday, and keep it after week 16.

milestones.title: Four weeks of the floor, held
milestones.criteria: Two lifts and a daily walk in every one of the first four weeks, lights out by 11 most nights, and four Sunday weigh-ins written down.

milestones.title: Halfway, and the lifts are heavier
milestones.criteria: Your main lift is up on where it started in week 1, and the Sunday trend has moved down across the month.

milestones.title: Held the line through the hard stretch
milestones.criteria: Weeks 10-13 done without a missed week — two lifts, daily walks, one plate at dinner.

milestones.title: 8 kg down, strength intact
milestones.criteria: Sunday weigh-in around 84 kg, and your main lift still at or above where it was in week 1.

steps.title: Set up the charging spot outside the bedroom

Plug the charger in there and leave it there
Put an alarm clock or your watch on the nightstand
Set the alarm on that clock, not the phone

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.body: A charger beside the bed means every boring moment at 11pm has a screen one reach away. A charger in the kitchen means getting to the scroll costs you a walk in the dark. That gap is the whole plan.

sections.heading: If you slip
sections.body: If the phone ends up back in the bedroom, don't argue with yourself about it — get up, walk it to its spot, come back. The walk is the fix, not the willpower.

how_to.counts_as_done: The charger is plugged in outside the bedroom and there's a clock by the bed.

steps.title: Off the sofa at 10:15pm
steps.details: Weeknights, 10:15pm is the handoff: up off the sofa, phone onto its charger in the other room, then into the bedroom. The sofa is where your night drifts — so the sofa is what we're ending early, not the scrolling.

how_to.gist: Up off the sofa at 10:15, phone to its charger, then to the bedroom.
how_to.why: You told me the drift starts on the sofa around 10 and finishes at 1am in bed. Cutting the sofa time short is how you stop the drift before it has a runway.

If you're mid-episode, pause it and leave it paused

sections.heading: If you slip

steps.details: Up at 6:30 on weekdays as you already are — and the same time on the weekend, within an hour. Alarm clock across the room so you have to stand up to kill it. A steady wake time is what makes 11pm feel like bedtime instead of a punishment.

how_to.gist: Up at 6:30 every day, alarm across the room so you stand up.
how_to.why: Your 6:30 work alarm is the strongest thing working for you. Keeping it steady — weekends included — is what pulls your whole night earlier without you having to fight for it.

Feet on the floor before you touch anything else

sections.body: Two long lie-ins and Monday night feels like jet lag — you're not tired at 11, you're wired, and the plan takes the hit. Keeping the wake time steady is the cheapest thing you can do for your nights.

sections.heading: If you slip
sections.body: Slept in on a Saturday? Don't try to make it up by going to bed early Sunday. Just take the normal 6:30-ish wake on Sunday and let Monday reset itself.

how_to.counts_as_done: You were up at your set time, alarm across the room, no snooze-in-bed.

steps.details: Last coffee, tea, cola or energy drink by 2pm. Caffeine hangs around for hours, and an afternoon cup is often why 11pm arrives and you're not remotely sleepy.

how_to.gist: Last coffee, tea or cola by 2pm.
how_to.why: If you're not sleepy at 11, the plan can't work — and a late-afternoon caffeine hit is the usual reason. This is the cheapest way to make 11pm feel like bedtime.

protocol.goal_statement: Build from ~8 clean push-ups to 30 unbroken push-ups in 8 weeks, training 4 mornings a week at home.
protocol.short_title: 30 push-ups in a row in 8 weeks

phases.title: Build the floor
phases.focus: Four short morning sets, every rep clean, and a written number for every set so next week has something to beat.

steps.title: 4 morning push-up sets
steps.details: Four mornings a week, at home, before the day starts. Each morning is 4 sets of 4 clean push-ups with 60-90 seconds rest between sets. Stop each set at the last rep you can do with a straight body and full lockout — never the last rep you could possibly force. 2-3 easy warm-up reps before the first working set. Total time: under 10 minutes.

how_to.gist: Four mornings a week: 4 sets of 4 clean push-ups, 60-90 seconds rest.
how_to.why: Your 8 dies on form, not strength. Four short sets done cleanly build the volume your max needs without ever teaching your body to grind out ugly reps — which is exactly how this goal usually dies.

sections.heading: The week
items: Wednesday, Saturday, Sunday — nothing. Rest is part of the plan.

sections.heading: Each set
sections.body: Hands just outside shoulder width, body in one straight line from head to heels, chest to a fist's height off the floor, then push all the way up to straight arms. Rest 60-90 seconds between sets — count it, don't guess. Two or three easy reps before your first working set to wake the shoulders up.

sections.heading: The rule
sections.body: The last rep of every set has to look like the first. If your hips sag, your head leads, or you only get halfway up, that rep doesn't count and the set is over. Four clean beats eight sloppy every single time.

sections.heading: If you slip
sections.body: Missed a morning? Do the next one. Two missed mornings in a row is the only thing that actually costs you here.

how_to.counts_as_done: 4 mornings done, 4 sets of 4 clean reps each, any order across the week.

steps.week_progression: Week 1: 4 sets of 4. Week 2: 4 sets of 5.

steps.title: Write down every set
steps.details: Right after each morning session, write the reps you actually got in each set in your phone notes — 4/4/4/4, or 5/4/4/3 if that's the truth. The honest number is the useful one. Next week you beat this week's numbers by one rep somewhere.

how_to.gist: After each session, note the reps you got in each set — honestly.
how_to.why: Push-up progress is invisible day to day. The written numbers are the only way you'll know the plan is working, and they're what tells you exactly when to add a rep and when to hold.

sections.heading: What to write
items: One word on how it felt — easy, solid, rough

sections.heading: Where
sections.body: Your phone's notes app, one note, newest entry at the top. Not a spreadsheet, not a training app — somewhere you'll actually open at 6:50am.

sections.heading: The point
sections.body: If every set reads 5/5/5/5 two sessions running, next session you go to 6. If sets are dropping off a cliff — 5/5/3/2 — you hold the same numbers next time instead of pushing.

how_to.counts_as_done: A written entry for each of the 4 sessions this week.

steps.week_progression: Same habit all 8 weeks — it's the thing that makes every other step work.

steps.title: Hit ~130 g protein a day
steps.details: Roughly 130 g of protein a day, spread across your three meals — a palm-sized portion of protein at each one: eggs, chicken, fish, Greek yogurt, beans, whatever you actually eat. You're not counting calories; you're making sure every meal has a real protein source in it.

how_to.gist: A palm of protein at every meal — roughly 130 g across the day.
how_to.why: Push-ups are a strength exercise, and strength gains need building material. Protein at every meal is the simplest version of that — no scales, no tracking app, just making sure no meal is protein-free.

sections.heading: The target
sections.body: About 130 g of protein a day, based on an assumed bodyweight of 170 lb. If that assumption is off, the number moves with it — tell the app your real weight and it'll recalculate.

sections.heading: What a palm looks like
items: 3 eggs, or a 5-egg omelette if you're hungry
A chicken breast or a salmon fillet
A big bowl of Greek yogurt with something in it
A scoop of protein powder in milk if a meal is rushed

sections.heading: The rule
sections.body: No meal without a protein source in it. That's the whole habit. Breakfast is the one most people skip it at, so that's the one to fix first.

how_to.counts_as_done: Three meals, three protein sources, every day.

steps.title: In bed by 10:45pm
steps.details: Lights out by 10:45pm so you get 7-8 hours before your morning session. Set an alarm for 10:15pm labelled 'start winding down' — phone on the charger across the room, not in bed. Recovery is where the reps you did actually turn into strength.

how_to.gist: Alarm at 10:15pm, lights out by 10:45pm, phone across the room.
how_to.why: You're training four mornings a week. Sore, under-slept shoulders don't add reps — they just make the next session harder. Sleep is the half of this plan that happens with your eyes shut.

sections.heading: The phone

sections.heading: Why it matters here

steps.title: Set up the floor the night before
steps.details: Before bed on the nights before a session, put your mat or towel down where you'll do the push-ups and lay out what you're wearing. Morning-you should be able to walk out and start with zero decisions to make.

how_to.gist: Mat down and clothes out the night before each morning session.
how_to.why: The gap between waking up and doing the first rep is where morning workouts die. Every decision you remove the night before is one less reason to skip it at 6:40am.

sections.heading: The morning

phases.title: Add the volume
phases.focus: More sets, longer holds at the top, and your first real max test — the numbers start climbing now.

steps.title: 5 morning push-up sets
steps.details: Same four mornings, now 5 sets instead of 4. Start at 5 reps per set and add a rep to one set per session as long as every set stays clean. Rest 60-90 seconds between sets. Still stop at the last clean rep, never the last possible one.

how_to.why: Your max is built from total clean reps, not from one heroic set. Adding a fifth set is the cheapest way to add volume without ever grinding.

sections.heading: Adding reps

sections.heading: The rule
sections.body: Same as always: the last rep has to look like the first. If it doesn't, the set is over and that rep doesn't count.

how_to.counts_as_done: 4 mornings done, 5 sets each, every set clean.

steps.week_progression: Week 3: 5 sets of 5-6. Week 4: 5 sets of 6-7.

steps.details: Same habit, more numbers to beat. Log each set's reps right after the session. This is what tells you whether to add a rep next time or hold.

how_to.gist: Log every set's reps right after each morning session.
how_to.why: You're adding reps now, and the log is the only thing that tells you whether the additions are working or whether you're just accumulating fatigue.

items: One word on how it felt

sections.body: Numbers holding steady or creeping up across the week: good, keep adding. Numbers dropping session to session: hold the same reps next time and let the shoulders catch up.

how_to.counts_as_done: A written entry for each of the 4 sessions this week.

steps.week_progression: Keep the same note going — by week 8 it's the whole story of this goal.

steps.title: Test your max
steps.details: Saturday of week 4, after a rest day: one all-out set of clean push-ups, no pacing, no stopping. Stop the moment form breaks — that's your number. Write it down. This is one of only two max tests in the whole plan.

how_to.gist: Saturday of week 4: one all-out clean set, stop when form breaks.
how_to.why: You need to know the real number to set the last four weeks correctly. Testing twice in eight weeks keeps the number honest without turning every session into a max attempt.

Stop the instant your form breaks

sections.heading: After

how_to.counts_as_done: One all-out clean set done and the number written down.

steps.week_progression: Only test in week 4 and week 8 — not before, not in between.

how_to.gist: A palm of protein at every meal — roughly 130 g a day.

phases.title: Push the ceiling
phases.focus: Longer sets, shorter rest, and the reps start coming in bigger blocks — this is where 30 stops being a theory.

steps.title: 4 mornings of long sets
steps.details: Four mornings, 4 sets each, but the sets are longer now — start at 8-10 reps per set and add one rep per set per week. Rest drops to 60 seconds. This is the phase that builds the endurance to hold a long unbroken set.

how_to.gist: Four mornings: 4 sets of 8-10 reps, 60 seconds rest.
how_to.why: Getting to 30 in a row isn't about getting stronger in short bursts — it's about holding form while tired. Longer sets with shorter rest is exactly that skill.

sections.heading: Adding reps
sections.body: Add one rep to each set each week — 8s become 9s, 9s become 10s. If a set falls apart before the target, hold that number next session rather than forcing it.

sections.heading: The rule
sections.body: Shorter rest makes this harder than it looks. If your form breaks in set 3, the answer is fewer reps in set 1 next time — not grinding through it.

how_to.counts_as_done: 4 mornings done, 4 sets each, all reps clean.

steps.week_progression: Week 5: 4 sets of 8-9. Week 6: 4 sets of 10-11.

steps.title: Write down every set
steps.details: Log each set's reps after every session. With sets this long, the log is how you spot the difference between a genuinely hard session and one you should have backed off on.

how_to.gist: Log every set's reps right after each morning session.
how_to.why: Long sets are where people accidentally overtrain. The log shows you the pattern before your shoulders do.

steps.title: One long unbroken set on Saturdays
steps.details: Saturday mornings, one set as far as you can go with clean form — no pacing, no stopping, no counting reps that don't count. Week 5 target: 15+ clean. Week 6 target: 20+ clean. This is practice for the real thing, not a test.

how_to.gist: Saturday: one unbroken set, as far as clean form allows.
how_to.why: The goal is 30 in a row, and the only way to get good at a long unbroken set is to do long unbroken sets. This is that practice, once a week, with a rest day before it.

sections.heading: How to do it
items: One set, all the way, no stopping

sections.heading: The rule
sections.body: If you hit 14 in week 5 with perfect form, that's a real 14 and it counts. Don't trade form for a number — the number you're chasing is 30 clean, and a sloppy 20 today buys you nothing.

how_to.counts_as_done: One unbroken set done Saturday, reps written down.

steps.week_progression: Week 5: 15+. Week 6: 20+.

phases.title: Go get the 30
phases.focus: Taper the volume, keep the quality, and take the one shot that counts.

steps.title: 3 mornings of sharp, short sets
steps.details: Down to three mornings — Monday, Wednesday, Friday. 3 sets of 8-10 clean reps, 90 seconds rest, done in under 10 minutes. Less volume on purpose: you're arriving at the final test fresh, not tired.

how_to.gist: Three mornings: 3 sets of 8-10 clean reps, 90 seconds rest.
how_to.why: You can't test a max on tired shoulders. Dropping to three short sessions keeps the movement sharp while letting the fatigue from six weeks of work drain away.

sections.heading: The rule
sections.body: Every rep clean, no exceptions. These sessions are about staying sharp, not about proving anything — the proving happens in week 8.

sections.heading: Week 8
sections.body: Same three sessions, but Monday and Wednesday only 2 sets of 8, and Friday is the test — so no session at all on the Friday of week 8.

how_to.counts_as_done: 3 sessions done this week, all reps clean.

steps.week_progression: Week 7: 3 sets of 8-10. Week 8: 2 sets of 8 on Monday and Wednesday, then rest into the test.

steps.title: Write down every set
steps.details: Keep logging, even in the taper. Fewer sessions means the log matters more — it's how you confirm you're staying sharp rather than losing ground.

how_to.gist: Log every set's reps after each of the three sessions.
how_to.why: The taper can feel like you're doing too little. The log is the evidence that you're not — the reps are still clean and the sets still feel solid.

sections.heading: What to write
items: One word on how it felt

sections.heading: What you're looking for
sections.body: Sets feeling easier than they did in week 6. That's the taper working — that's what fresh feels like.

how_to.counts_as_done: A written entry for each of the 3 sessions this week.

steps.week_progression: Last two weeks of the note — it's nearly the whole story now.

steps.title: Test your max

how_to.gist: Saturday of week 8: one all-out set. Stop when form breaks.
how_to.why: This is the whole point of the eight weeks. Everything before now was building toward one honest set, done fresh, with no excuses either way.

how_to.counts_as_done: One all-out clean set done and the number written down.

steps.week_progression: One shot, week 8, Saturday. That's it.

how_to.gist: Lights out by 10:45pm, phone across the room — especially Friday night.
how_to.why: The test is Saturday morning. A full night's sleep on Friday is worth more reps than any extra set you could squeeze in during the week.

milestones.title: Two weeks, eight mornings, zero skipped
milestones.criteria: You completed all 8 sessions across weeks 1 and 2, every set stopped at the last clean rep, and every set is written down.

milestones.title: First real number
milestones.criteria: You tested your max on the Saturday of week 4 and wrote down an honest, clean number — whatever it was. If it's higher than 8, the plan is working exactly as designed.

milestones.title: Past 20 in one go
milestones.criteria: You completed a Saturday unbroken set of 20 or more clean reps, and you've held four mornings a week for six straight weeks.

milestones.title: 30 in a row
milestones.criteria: One all-out set on the Saturday of week 8, stopped at the last clean rep. 30 or more means you hit the goal; anything above 20 is a genuine transformation from where you started.

protocol.coach_notes: You came in knowing your real number and exactly where it breaks down — that's rarer than you'd think, and it's why this plan can be this specific. The whole thing rests on one rule: every set ends at the last clean rep, never the last possible one. That rule is why you'll still have working shoulders in week 8. One missed morning is noise; it's the morning after a miss that decides whether this happens, so if you skip one, the next one is the whole game. See you at 30.

sessions.goal: Hold a basic 5-minute conversation in Spanish within 3 month

protocol.goal_statement: Hold a basic 5-minute conversation in Spanish in 12 weeks, starting from ~20 words, using 30 minutes each morning plus your partner as a live practice partner.
protocol.short_title: Hold a 5-minute Spanish conversation in 12 weeks

phases.title: Thirty words, out loud
phases.focus: Build the morning slot and get your first real sentences spoken to your partner — even terrible ones.

steps.title: 30 minutes of Spanish before work
steps.details: Same chair, same time, before you do anything else. Ten minutes of new words, ten minutes saying them out loud, ten minutes listening to slow Spanish and repeating what you hear. Phone on the table, not in your hand.

how_to.gist: Same chair, same time, 30 minutes before work — six mornings a week.
how_to.why: Thirty minutes a morning is the whole engine of this goal. It doesn't need to be more, and it does need to actually happen, so the slot is fixed and the decision is already made.

sections.heading: The slot
sections.body: Before work, before your phone, before coffee if that's what it takes. The chair and the time stay the same every day so starting costs you nothing.

sections.heading: The 30 minutes
items: 10 minutes of new words — write them, say them
10 minutes saying full sentences out loud
10 minutes listening to slow Spanish and repeating it back

sections.heading: If it goes badly
sections.body: Some mornings nothing will stick. Sit the 30 minutes anyway and move on. The sitting is the rep, not the remembering.

how_to.counts_as_done: 30 minutes done at the morning slot, six mornings this week.

steps.week_progression: Weeks 1-3: keep it to 30 minutes. Do not add time — add consistency.

steps.title: Say your 20 words out loud from memory
steps.details: At the end of each morning session, close everything and say the words you know out loud without looking. Add two or three new ones each day. By week three you should be past forty words you can produce without help.

how_to.gist: Close the book and say what you know out loud, no looking.
how_to.why: Recognising a word on a screen and being able to say it in a conversation are two different skills. This is the one that turns into speech.

sections.heading: How
sections.body: Everything closed. Say every word you can remember out loud, then add two or three new ones. If you get stuck, that's the word you practise tomorrow.

sections.heading: The target
sections.body: You start with about twenty words. Two or three a day for three weeks puts you past forty you can say without help.

how_to.counts_as_done: Words said out loud from memory, no notes, at the end of the morning session.

steps.week_progression: Weeks 1-3: two or three new words a day. Don't chase a big number — chase words you can actually say.

steps.title: One sentence about your actual day, spoken
steps.details: Before you finish the morning session, say one true sentence about your day in Spanish — what you're doing, what you ate, how you slept. Wrong is fine. Out loud is not optional.

how_to.gist: One true sentence about your day, out loud, before you stop.
how_to.why: Words on their own don't become conversation. One real sentence a day is how you start building the thing you're actually chasing.

sections.heading: The rule
sections.body: It has to be true and it has to be out loud. "Hoy trabajo mucho." "El café está frío." That's a sentence. That counts.

sections.heading: Don't polish it
sections.body: Say it once, badly, and move on. You are not writing an essay, you are getting your mouth used to the language.

how_to.counts_as_done: One spoken sentence about your real day, said out loud before the session ended.

steps.week_progression: Weeks 1-3: one sentence. From week 4 this grows into the two-minute stretch.

steps.title: Sunday conversation with your partner
steps.details: Ten minutes, no English allowed from you — your partner can drop into English if you're truly stuck. Greetings, how the week went, what you're doing today. Same time every Sunday so it's a standing appointment, not a favour you have to ask for.

how_to.gist: Ten minutes of Spanish with your partner every Sunday, same time.
how_to.why: A live speaker at home is the single biggest advantage you have over every app-only learner. This is where the words you've been drilling turn into an actual exchange.

sections.heading: The setup
sections.body: Same time every Sunday, ten minutes, somewhere you can both sit down. Standing appointment, not something you have to negotiate each week.

sections.heading: The rule
sections.body: You stay in Spanish. Your partner can rescue you with English if you're genuinely stuck, but you don't reach for it first. Getting stuck and working around it is the practice.

sections.heading: What to talk about
items: Greetings and how the week went
One thing you learned this week
Anything you can't say — write it down and bring it back next Sunday

how_to.counts_as_done: Ten minutes of Spanish with your partner on Sunday, you speaking Spanish throughout.

steps.week_progression: Weeks 1-3: ten minutes. It will feel short and clumsy — that's the point at this stage.

steps.title: Spanish ready before you sit down
steps.details: The night before, put your notebook, your word list and your headphones on the chair you'll sit in. Nothing to find, nothing to decide, nothing to charge in the morning.

how_to.gist: Set out your notebook, word list and headphones the night before.
how_to.why: The mornings you skip are the ones where you had to go looking for something first. Removing that step is the cheapest way to protect the slot.

sections.heading: The night before
items: Notebook and pen on the chair
Word list on top of the notebook
Headphones out of the case and charged
Phone alarm set for the same time as always

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.body: Every decision you remove from the morning is a decision you can't get wrong at 6:40am. This takes ninety seconds the night before and saves the whole session.

how_to.counts_as_done: Everything laid out the night before, ready for the morning session.

steps.week_progression: Weeks 1-3: every night before a morning session. This is what keeps the slot alive.

phases.title: Building sentences that hold
phases.focus: Move from single words to short exchanges, and start bringing back what you learned in week one instead of only adding new material.

steps.title: 30 minutes of Spanish before work
steps.details: Same slot, same 30 minutes, but the mix shifts: ten minutes of new material, ten minutes of going back over last week's words and sentences, ten minutes speaking out loud.

how_to.gist: Same 30 minutes, but a third of it now goes back over old material.
how_to.why: Adding new words every day while never revisiting the old ones is how people end up with a hundred words they can't use. The review third is what makes them stick.

sections.heading: The review rule
sections.body: Anything you got wrong yesterday gets said out loud first today. Old material before new material, every morning.

how_to.counts_as_done: 30 minutes done, including the review third.

steps.week_progression: Weeks 4-6: the review third is non-negotiable. This is where the early weeks start paying off.

steps.title: Two minutes of unbroken speech
steps.details: At the end of the morning session, talk out loud for two minutes without stopping and without English. About your day, your plans, what's in the room. Silence is fine — pause, then keep going.

how_to.gist: Two minutes of talking out loud, no stopping, no English.
how_to.why: Five minutes of conversation is the goal, and you get there by stretching the unbroken stretch a little at a time. Two minutes is the next step up from one sentence.

sections.heading: How
sections.body: Talk about anything real — your day, your plans, what's in front of you. If you run out of words, pause and start a new sentence. The clock keeps running.

sections.heading: The rule
sections.body: No English, no writing, no looking things up. Two minutes of whatever Spanish you have, even if it's clumsy.

how_to.counts_as_done: Two minutes of continuous spoken Spanish, no English.

steps.week_progression: Weeks 4-6: two minutes. From week 7 this becomes three.

steps.title: Sunday conversation with your partner
steps.details: Fifteen minutes now, and you open it. Bring three questions you prepared during the week and ask them. Your partner answers, you follow up with one more question each time.

how_to.gist: Fifteen minutes Sunday, and you're the one asking the questions.
how_to.why: Asking questions is what keeps a conversation going past the first exchange. If you only ever answer, five minutes will feel like a wall.

sections.heading: Before Sunday
sections.body: Write three questions during the week — anything you'd genuinely want to know. Bring them written down.

sections.heading: During
sections.body: You ask, they answer, you ask one follow-up. That follow-up is the part that matters — it's what turns an interview into a conversation.

how_to.counts_as_done: Fifteen minutes of Spanish on Sunday, with you asking your three prepared questions.

steps.week_progression: Weeks 4-6: fifteen minutes, you leading. Weeks 7-9: twenty minutes.

steps.title: Write down what you couldn't say
steps.details: Right after the Sunday conversation, write down every word or phrase you reached for and didn't have. Those go to the top of Monday morning's session — they're the most useful words you'll learn all week.

how_to.gist: After Sunday, write down everything you couldn't say — it's Monday's material.
how_to.why: The gaps you hit in real conversation are exactly the words you need next. Learning them cold from a list is far slower than learning them because you wanted them.

sections.heading: Right after
sections.body: Two minutes, while it's fresh. Every word you wanted and didn't have, in English if you have to.

sections.heading: Then what
sections.body: Monday morning starts with those words. Say them out loud, use them in a sentence, and bring them back next Sunday.

how_to.counts_as_done: A written list of the gaps from Sunday's conversation, ready for Monday.

steps.week_progression: Weeks 4-6: every Sunday. This list is what makes the following week's study personal.

steps.title: Spanish ready before you sit down
steps.details: Same night-before setup: notebook, word list, headphones on the chair. Add one thing — the list of gaps from Sunday's conversation goes on top.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 4-6: every night before a morning session.

phases.title: Holding the thread
phases.focus: Push the unbroken stretch toward five minutes and start handling the moments where you don't understand what was said to you.

steps.title: 30 minutes of Spanish before work
steps.details: Same slot. Ten minutes new material, ten minutes review, ten minutes speaking — but the speaking ten is now mostly listening to a short clip and answering it out loud.

how_to.gist: Same 30 minutes, but the speaking ten is now answering real audio.
how_to.why: Conversation is half listening. Answering a clip out loud is the closest thing to a live exchange you can do alone at 6:40am.

sections.heading: The new mix
items: 10 minutes answering a short audio clip out loud

sections.heading: The clip
sections.body: One or two minutes of slow Spanish, played twice. Then you answer it out loud as if someone had asked you directly.

how_to.counts_as_done: 30 minutes done, including the audio-answer ten.

steps.week_progression: Weeks 7-9: the audio-answer ten replaces the plain speaking ten.

steps.title: Three minutes of unbroken speech
steps.details: Three minutes now, still no English, still no stopping. Pick a topic before you start — your week, a film, a plan — so you're not inventing it as you go.

how_to.gist: Three minutes out loud on a topic you picked in advance.
how_to.why: Picking the topic first is what makes this feel like talking rather than scrambling. It's the same move you'll make in a real conversation.

sections.heading: How
sections.body: Choose the topic in ten seconds, then talk. Three minutes, no English, no notes. Pause when you need to, then keep going.

sections.heading: If you dry up
sections.body: Say "no sé cómo decir esto" and keep talking around it. Working around a gap is a real conversational skill, not a failure.

how_to.counts_as_done: Three minutes of continuous spoken Spanish on a chosen topic.

steps.week_progression: Weeks 7-9: three minutes. Weeks 10-12: five.

steps.title: Sunday conversation with your partner
steps.details: Twenty minutes. Your partner now speaks at normal speed and doesn't slow down for you. When you don't understand, you ask them to repeat or say it differently — in Spanish.

how_to.gist: Twenty minutes Sunday at normal speed, and you ask for repeats in Spanish.
how_to.why: Real conversation doesn't come slowed down. Learning to say "otra vez, más despacio" keeps a conversation alive when you miss something — which you will.

sections.heading: The change
sections.body: Normal speed from your partner. No slowing down, no simplifying. You handle the gaps.

sections.heading: The point
sections.body: Missing things and recovering is the actual skill. A conversation where you understood everything isn't practice, it's a performance.

how_to.counts_as_done: Twenty minutes of Spanish on Sunday at normal speed, with you asking for repeats when needed.

steps.week_progression: Weeks 7-9: twenty minutes at normal speed. Weeks 10-12: twenty-five.

steps.details: Same as before, but now also note the phrases you needed to ask for a repeat or a rephrase. Those are the ones that keep you in the conversation.

how_to.gist: After Sunday, write down the gaps — including the phrases you used to recover.
how_to.why: The recovery phrases are the ones that stop a conversation from ending. Noting them means you'll have them ready next time.

sections.heading: Right after
sections.body: Two minutes. Words you wanted, and the moments you got lost and how you got back.

sections.heading: Then what
sections.body: Monday morning starts with this list. Say each one out loud in a sentence before you touch anything new.

how_to.counts_as_done: Gap list written, including the phrases you used to recover.

steps.week_progression: Weeks 7-9: every Sunday.

steps.title: Spanish ready before you sit down
steps.details: Night-before setup, unchanged: notebook, word list, gap list on top, headphones charged. By now this should take you under a minute.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 7-9: every night before a morning session.

phases.title: Five minutes, start to finish
phases.focus: Run the full five minutes end to end, several times, until it stops being an event and starts being a conversation.

steps.title: 30 minutes of Spanish before work
steps.details: Same slot, same 30 minutes. The new-material ten shrinks to five and the speaking ten grows to fifteen — at this stage, using what you have beats collecting more.

how_to.gist: Same 30 minutes, but more of it is speaking and less is new words.
how_to.why: Twelve weeks in, you have enough words for five minutes. The last stretch is about using them fluently, not adding more.

sections.heading: Why less new material
sections.body: A word you can use beats three you can only recognise. The last three weeks are about fluency with what you already have.

how_to.counts_as_done: 30 minutes done, with the speaking fifteen.

steps.week_progression: Weeks 10-12: hold this mix. No new additions.

steps.title: Five minutes of unbroken speech
steps.details: The full five minutes, alone, out loud, no English. This is the target distance — you're rehearsing the exact thing you're going to do with your partner on Sunday.

how_to.gist: Five minutes out loud, alone, no English — the full target distance.
how_to.why: This is the goal, rehearsed daily. By the time you do it with your partner it should feel like something you've already done many times.

sections.heading: How
sections.body: Five minutes, out loud, no English, no notes. Topic of your choosing. If you stall, work around it and keep the clock running.

sections.heading: The point
sections.body: You're not performing for anyone. You're making five minutes of Spanish feel ordinary so that Sunday doesn't feel like an exam.

how_to.counts_as_done: Five continuous minutes of spoken Spanish, no English.

steps.week_progression: Weeks 10-12: five minutes every morning. This is the ceiling — hold it.

steps.title: Sunday five-minute conversation, timed
steps.details: Five minutes, timed, start to finish, no English from you. Then keep going for the rest of your usual twenty-five minutes if it's flowing — the timed five is the target, the rest is bonus.

how_to.gist: Five timed minutes with your partner, no English from you.
how_to.why: This is the goal itself. Doing it timed, on a Sunday, with the person you actually want to talk to, is the whole point of the last twelve weeks.

sections.heading: The five
sections.body: Set a timer, start talking, don't stop and don't switch to English. Greetings, how the week went, plans, anything. Five minutes.

sections.heading: After the five
sections.body: If it's still going, keep going. The timed five is the target; everything past it is free.

sections.heading: If it falls apart
sections.body: Try again next Sunday. One bad five minutes doesn't undo eleven weeks — the next one is what counts.

how_to.counts_as_done: Five timed minutes of Spanish with your partner, no English from you.

steps.week_progression: Weeks 10-12: one timed five each Sunday. Three clean ones and you've done it.

steps.title: Write down what you couldn't say
steps.details: Keep the list going. At this stage it's mostly words you know but couldn't reach for in time — those are the ones worth drilling on Monday.

how_to.gist: Keep the gap list going — mostly words you knew but couldn't reach in time.
how_to.why: Late-stage gaps are retrieval problems, not knowledge problems. Naming them is how you fix them.

sections.heading: Right after
sections.body: Two minutes. Words you knew and couldn't reach for, plus anything genuinely new.

sections.heading: Then what
sections.body: Monday morning, say each one out loud in a sentence before anything else.

how_to.counts_as_done: Gap list written after Sunday's conversation.

milestones.title: Three weeks of mornings, unbroken
milestones.criteria: You've done the 30-minute morning session six days a week for three straight weeks, and you can say forty-plus words out loud without looking.

milestones.title: You're asking the questions
milestones.criteria: You've run three Sunday conversations where you asked your own prepared questions and followed up, and you can talk for two minutes straight without English.

milestones.title: You can get lost and get back
milestones.criteria: You've held a twenty-minute conversation at normal speed and asked for a repeat or a rephrase in Spanish instead of switching to English.

milestones.title: Five minutes, start to finish
milestones.criteria: You've held a timed five-minute conversation in Spanish with your partner, no English from you, and done it at least three times.

protocol.coach_notes: Weeks one to three will feel like nothing is landing. It is landing — that feeling is what the first month of a language always feels like, and it's the exact point where most people stop. The mornings you least want to sit down are the ones that decide this. And if you miss a day, don't miss the next one: one skipped morning is noise, the morning after it is the whole habit. You have something most learners never get — someone at home who speaks the language. Use them early and often, even when your Spanish is bad. Especially then.
